The first: When He, the Exalted, guided the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) to adhering to the religion agreed upon, He made clear that He guided them to this good only because He chose them, selected them, and singled them out with abundant mercy and honor.

The second: The call of the messengers was burdensome for them only because of the submission it required to them out of arrogance and pride. So He, the Exalted, made clear that He singles out whom He wills with the messengership, and submission to them is obligatory. Lineage, ancestry and wealth are not taken into account; rather all are equal in that they are obligated to follow the messengers whom Allah, the Exalted, has chosen. The derivation of the word "ijtiba'" (choosing) indicates gathering and collecting, from which comes "jaba al-kharaj" (he collected the tax) and "jaba al-ma'a fi al-hawd" (he gathered the water into the basin). So His saying ﴿Allah chooses for Himself﴾ means He gathers him to Himself and brings him close with the nearness of honor and mercy. His saying ﴿whom He wills﴾ is like His saying: ﴿He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills﴾ [al-Ankabut: 21].

* * *

Then He said: ﴿and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance﴾. This is, as has been related in the report: "Whoever draws near to Me a handspan, I draw near to him an arm's length; and whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running." That is: whoever turns toward Him with obedience, He turns toward him with His guidance and direction, by expanding his breast and facilitating his affair.

Know that when He, the Exalted, made clear that He commanded all the prophets and nations to adhere to the religion agreed upon, someone could say: "Then why do we find them divided?" So Allah, the Exalted, answered on their behalf by His saying: ﴿And they did not divide except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves.﴾ He means: they did not divide except after they knew that division is misguidance; but they did so out of envy and the pursuit of leadership. Natural zeal and innate pride drove each group to adopt a doctrine, call people to it, and disparage whatever else was other than it, seeking fame and leadership. This became the cause of the occurrence of disagreement. Then He, the Exalted, informed us that they deserved punishment because of this act. However, He, the Exalted, delayed that punishment from them, because for every punishment with Him there is a specified term, that is, a known time, either for the sheer exercise of His will, as is our position, or because He knew that the good lies in its realization at that time, as the Mu'tazilah hold. This is the meaning of His saying ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord for a specified term, the matter would have been decided between them.﴾ The specified term may be in this world or in the Resurrection. The commentators differed about those who are meant by this description. Most said: They are the Jews and the Christians. The evidence is His saying in Al 'Imran: ﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves﴾ [Al 'Imran: 19], and His saying in the surah "Lam yakun": ﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not divide except after the clear evidence had come to them﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 4]. Also, His saying ﴿except after knowledge had come to them﴾ is fitting for the People of the Book.

Others said: They are the Arabs. This is false, for the reasons mentioned. His saying, the Exalted, after this verse ﴿And indeed, those who were given the Scripture after them﴾ does not befit the Arabs, because "those who were given the Scripture after them" are the People of the Book who were in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ﴿are in disquieting doubt concerning it﴾, concerning their own Book, ﴿disquieting﴾, not believing in it with true faith.

* * *

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So for that, invite, and remain steadfast as you were commanded﴾. That is: for the sake of that division, and for the sake of the many disagreements that arose in the religion, invite people to agreement upon the upright monotheistic faith (al-millah al-hanifiyyah), remain steadfast upon it and upon calling to it as Allah commanded you, and do not follow their divergent, false desires. ﴿And say: "I believe in whatever Allah has sent down of Scripture"﴾, that is, in whatever Scripture it is established that Allah sent down. That means belief in all the revealed books, because those who divided believed in some and disbelieved in others. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿We believe in some and disbelieve in others﴾ [al-Nisa': 150], up to His saying ﴿those are the disbelievers in truth﴾ [al-Nisa': 151]. Then He said: ﴿And I was commanded to act justly between you﴾, that is, in judgment, when you dispute and bring your disputes to me for judgment. Al-Qaffal said: its meaning is that my Lord commanded me not to distinguish between myself and yourselves, by commanding you to do what I do not do, or by opposing you in what I have forbidden you; rather I treat you equally with myself. Likewise I treat your great ones and your small ones equally in matters that concern the judgment of Allah.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. There is no argument between us and you. Allah will bring us together, and to Him is the final return.﴾

The meaning is that the God of all is one, and each person is specifically responsible for his own deeds. Therefore each person must occupy himself in this world with his own self, for God will gather all of them together on the Day of Resurrection and recompense each one for his deeds. The intended purpose of this is disengagement (al-mutarakah) and each person's occupation with his own important matters. If it is said: how does what was done to them of killing, destruction of their houses, cutting down of palm trees, and expulsion befit this disengagement? We say: this disengagement was conditional upon their accepting the religion whose soundness is agreed upon among all the prophets, which includes monotheism (al-tawhid), abandoning the worship of idols, affirming the prophethood of the prophets, and affirming the truth of the resurrection and the Last Day. When they did not accept this religion, the condition was then unfulfilled, and therefore the conditioned matter was unfulfilled.

* * *

First: this statement is mentioned in the context of disputation. If the intended meaning of this verse were the prohibition of disputation, it would follow that it is prohibited in itself, and this is contradictory.

Second: were it not for the proofs, obligation would not have been directed.

Rather, the intended meaning is that the people recognized by the proof the truth of Muhammad (ﷺ), and they only abandoned affirming him out of rebellion and obstinacy. So God, exalted is He, made clear that the need to dispute with them has been eliminated, because they have recognized his truth through the proof; so there is no need whatsoever to dispute with them. One kind is that to which the introduction of abrogation (naskh) and change is impossible; rather it remains obligatory in all laws and religions, such as the view that truthfulness, justice and benevolence are good, and the view that lying, injustice and harming others are ugly.

The other kind is that which differs with the difference of laws and religions. This verse indicates that the legislator's effort to establish the first kind is stronger than his effort to establish the second kind, because persistence in the first kind is important for acquiring the states that bring about happiness in the Hereafter.

The third issue: His, the Exalted, saying ﴿that you establish the religion and do not divide over it﴾ indicates that attaining agreement is a demanded matter in both the Law and reason. The explanation of its benefit is in several aspects:

The first: Souls have influences, and when souls agree and concur upon one thing, the influence becomes strong.

The second: When they concur, each one of them becomes a helper to the other in that specific aim, and the multiplicity of helpers brings about the attainment of the aim. But when they differ, they dispute and argue, and so they weaken, and the aim is not attained.

The third: The occurrence of dispute is contrary to the interest of the world, because it leads to chaos (al-harj wa-al-maraj), killing and plunder. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, commanded in this verse the establishment of the religion in a way that does not lead to division, and He said in another verse: ﴿And do not dispute, lest you lose courage﴾ [al-Anfal: 46].

* * *

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance﴾. There are two interpretations of this:

The first: When He, the Exalted, guided the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) to adhering to the religion agreed upon, He made clear that He guided them to this good only because He chose them, selected them, and singled them out with abundant mercy and honor.

The second: The call of the messengers was burdensome for them only because of the submission it required to them out of arrogance and pride. So He, the Exalted, made clear that He singles out whom He wills with the messengership, and submission to them is obligatory. Lineage, ancestry and wealth are not taken into account; rather all are equal in that they are obligated to follow the messengers whom Allah, the Exalted, has chosen. The derivation of the word "ijtiba'" (choosing) indicates gathering and collecting, from which comes "jaba al-kharaj" (he collected the tax) and "jaba al-ma'a fi al-hawd" (he gathered the water into the basin). So His saying ﴿Allah chooses for Himself﴾ means He gathers him to Himself and brings him close with the nearness of honor and mercy. His saying ﴿whom He wills﴾ is like His saying: ﴿He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills﴾ [al-Ankabut: 21].

* * *

Then He said: ﴿and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance﴾. This is, as has been related in the report: "Whoever draws near to Me a handspan, I draw near to him an arm's length; and whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running." That is: whoever turns toward Him with obedience, He turns toward him with His guidance and direction, by expanding his breast and facilitating his affair.

Know that when He, the Exalted, made clear that He commanded all the prophets and nations to adhere to the religion agreed upon, someone could say: "Then why do we find them divided?" So Allah, the Exalted, answered on their behalf by His saying: ﴿And they did not divide except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves.﴾ He means: they did not divide except after they knew that division is misguidance; but they did so out of envy and the pursuit of leadership. Natural zeal and innate pride drove each group to adopt a doctrine, call people to it, and disparage whatever else was other than it, seeking fame and leadership. This became the cause of the occurrence of disagreement. Then He, the Exalted, informed us that they deserved punishment because of this act. However, He, the Exalted, delayed that punishment from them, because for every punishment with Him there is a specified term, that is, a known time, either for the sheer exercise of His will, as is our position, or because He knew that the good lies in its realization at that time, as the Mu'tazilah hold. This is the meaning of His saying ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord for a specified term, the matter would have been decided between them.﴾ The specified term may be in this world or in the Resurrection. The commentators differed about those who are meant by this description. Most said: They are the Jews and the Christians. The evidence is His saying in Al 'Imran: ﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves﴾ [Al 'Imran: 19], and His saying in the surah "Lam yakun": ﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not divide except after the clear evidence had come to them﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 4]. Also, His saying ﴿except after knowledge had come to them﴾ is fitting for the People of the Book.

Others said: They are the Arabs. This is false, for the reasons mentioned. His saying, the Exalted, after this verse ﴿And indeed, those who were given the Scripture after them﴾ does not befit the Arabs, because "those who were given the Scripture after them" are the People of the Book who were in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ﴿are in disquieting doubt concerning it﴾, concerning their own Book, ﴿disquieting﴾, not believing in it with true faith.

* * *

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So for that, invite, and remain steadfast as you were commanded﴾. That is: for the sake of that division, and for the sake of the many disagreements that arose in the religion, invite people to agreement upon the upright monotheistic faith (al-millah al-hanifiyyah), remain steadfast upon it and upon calling to it as Allah commanded you, and do not follow their divergent, false desires. ﴿And say: "I believe in whatever Allah has sent down of Scripture"﴾, that is, in whatever Scripture it is established that Allah sent down. That means belief in all the revealed books, because those who divided believed in some and disbelieved in others. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿We believe in some and disbelieve in others﴾ [al-Nisa': 150], up to His saying ﴿those are the disbelievers in truth﴾ [al-Nisa': 151]. Then He said: ﴿And I was commanded to act justly between you﴾, that is, in judgment, when you dispute and bring your disputes to me for judgment. Al-Qaffal said: its meaning is that my Lord commanded me not to distinguish between myself and yourselves, by commanding you to do what I do not do, or by opposing you in what I have forbidden you; rather I treat you equally with myself. Likewise I treat your great ones and your small ones equally in matters that concern the judgment of Allah.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. There is no argument between us and you. Allah will bring us together, and to Him is the final return.﴾

[p. 137]

The meaning is that the God of all is one, and each person is specifically responsible for his own deeds. Therefore each person must occupy himself in this world with his own self, for God will gather all of them together on the Day of Resurrection and recompense each one for his deeds. The intended purpose of this is disengagement (al-mutarakah) and each person's occupation with his own important matters. If it is said: how does what was done to them of killing, destruction of their houses, cutting down of palm trees, and expulsion befit this disengagement? We say: this disengagement was conditional upon their accepting the religion whose soundness is agreed upon among all the prophets, which includes monotheism (al-tawhid), abandoning the worship of idols, affirming the prophethood of the prophets, and affirming the truth of the resurrection and the Last Day. When they did not accept this religion, the condition was then unfulfilled, and therefore the conditioned matter was unfulfilled.

* * *

Know that the intended meaning of His words ﴿There is no argument between us and you﴾ is not the prohibition of what is similar to their disputation. Several points show this:

First: this statement is mentioned in the context of disputation. If the intended meaning of this verse were the prohibition of disputation, it would follow that it is prohibited in itself, and this is contradictory.

Second: were it not for the proofs, obligation would not have been directed.

Third: proof produces knowledge, and that cannot be prohibited. Rather, the intended meaning is that the people recognized by the proof the truth of Muhammad (ﷺ), and they only abandoned affirming him out of rebellion and obstinacy. So God, exalted is He, made clear that the need to dispute with them has been eliminated, because they have recognized his truth through the proof; so there is no need whatsoever to dispute with them. Among what strengthens our view that disputation cannot be prohibited is His words ﴿And argue with them in the best manner﴾ [al-Nahl: 125], His words ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in the best manner﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 46], His words ﴿O Noah, you have disputed with us and multiplied our disputation﴾ [Hud: 32], and His words ﴿And that was Our argument which We gave to Abraham against his people﴾ [al-An'am: 83].

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who argue about God﴾, i.e., dispute concerning His religion, ﴿after it has been responded to﴾, i.e., after people have responded to that religion, ﴿their argument is baseless﴾, i.e., false. That dispute was that the Jews said: Do you not say that adhering to what is agreed upon is better than adhering to what is disputed? The prophethood of Moses and the truth of the Torah are known by consensus, while the prophethood of Muhammad is not agreed upon. So if you build your speech in this verse on the premise that adhering to what is agreed upon is better, then it must be that Judaism is better to adhere to. God, exalted is He, then made clear that this argument is baseless, i.e., false and corrupt. That is because the Jews agreed that faith in Moses, peace be upon him, was obligatory only because of the manifestation of miracles in accordance with his claim, and here miracles manifested in accordance with the claim of Muhammad, peace be upon him, and the Jews witnessed those miracles. If the manifestation of a miracle indicates truthfulness, then here it is obligatory to acknowledge the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ); and if it does not indicate truthfulness, then it would be obligatory regarding Moses that they not acknowledge his prophethood. As for acknowledging the prophethood of Moses while persisting in denying the prophethood of Muhammad, despite both being equal in the manifestation of miracles, this is contradictory.

When God established these proofs, He warned the deniers with the punishment of the Resurrection, saying: ﴿It is God who revealed the Book with truth and the Balance. And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾. The meaning is: God, exalted is He, revealed the Book which contains various kinds of proofs and clear evidences, and revealed the Balance, which is the criterion that is the upright scale, and that they do not know when the Resurrection will suddenly come upon them. Since this is the case, it is obligatory for the rational person to strive and exert effort in reflection and reasoning, and to abandon the way of the people of ignorance and blind imitation. Since the Messenger was threatening them with the descent of the Resurrection and repeated this a great deal, and they saw no effect of it, they said in mockery: When will the Resurrection occur? Would that it occurred so that it would become clear to us that the truth is what we are upon, or what Muhammad and his companions are upon. To dispel this doubt, God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, but those who believe are apprehensive of it﴾. The meaning is clear. They are apprehensive and fearful only because they know that at its occurrence repentance is impossible; as for the denier of resurrection, it is so that this fear does not occur to him.

Then He said: ﴿Unquestionably, those who dispute about the Hour are in extreme error﴾. Al-mumara is persistent contention. Al-Zajjaj said: those into whom doubt and uncertainty about the occurrence of the Hour enter, so they dispute about it and deny it. ﴿Are in extreme error﴾ because the restoration of the oppressed person's right from the oppressor is obligatory in justice; so if the Resurrection did not occur, it would follow that injustice is attributed to God, exalted is He, and this is among the most absurd impossibilities; therefore denying the Resurrection is indeed extreme error.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿God is Subtle with His servants﴾, i.e., abundantly beneficent toward them. The mention of this statement here is appropriate because He revealed to them the Book containing these subtle proofs, so that was among God's subtle kindness to His servants. Also, those who disbelieved deserved severe punishment, yet God deferred that punishment from them, and that too is among God's subtle kindness. Since the bringing of the greatest benefits to them and the warding off of the greatest harms from them had been mentioned, it is therefore fitting that it be mentioned here. Then He said: ﴿He provides for whom He wills﴾, meaning that the root of beneficence and goodness is general with respect to all servants, and that is beneficence through life, reason, and understanding, and the granting of what is indispensable of provision, and the warding off of most calamities and afflictions from them. As for the degrees of bounty and delight, they vary and differ.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And He is the Strong﴾, i.e., the Able over everything He wills, ﴿the Mighty﴾, who cannot be overcome or resisted.

Hard for the polytheists is that to which you call them. Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance.﴾ ﴿And they did not divide except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord for a specified term, the matter would have been decided between them. And say: "I believe in whatever Allah has sent down of Scripture, and I was commanded to act justly between you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. There is no argument between us and you. Allah will bring us together, and to Him is the final return."﴾ ﴿And those who argue about Allah after He has been responded to, their argument is baseless with their Lord, and upon them is anger, and for them is a severe punishment.﴾ ﴿It is Allah who has sent down the Book in truth, and the balance. And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.﴾ ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe fear it and know that it is the truth. Unquestionably, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in far error.﴾ ﴿Allah is Subtle with His servants; He provides for whom He wills, and He is the Strong, the Mighty.﴾

Know that when He, the Exalted, magnified His revelation to Muhammad (ﷺ) by His saying: ﴿Thus He reveals to you, and to those before you, Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [al-Shura: 3], He then mentioned in this verse the detail of that. He said: ﴿He has ordained for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah.﴾ The meaning is: He has ordained for you, O companions of Muhammad, of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah, Muhammad, Abraham, Moses and Jesus. This is the intended meaning of the wording of the verse. He specifically mentioned these five prophets because they are the greatest of the prophets, the possessors of the great laws and the numerous followers. However, there remain difficulties in the wording of the verse.

The first: He said at the beginning of the verse ﴿what He enjoined upon Noah﴾, and at its end ﴿and what We enjoined upon Abraham﴾, and in the middle ﴿and what We revealed to you﴾. So what is the benefit of this variation?

The second: He mentioned Noah (peace be upon him) in the third person, saying ﴿what He enjoined upon Noah﴾, while the other two parts are in the first person plural, saying ﴿and what We revealed to you and what We enjoined upon Abraham﴾.

The third: The sense of the verse becomes: "Allah has ordained for you of the religion that which We revealed to you." So His saying ﴿He has ordained for you﴾ is addressed in the third person, while His saying ﴿what We revealed to you﴾ is addressed in the second person. This requires combining address in the third person and address in the second person in a single utterance under a single consideration, and this is problematic. These difficulties must be investigated, and the people [i.e., the commentators] have not revolved around them.

In sum, the purpose of the verse is that it is said: "He has ordained for you of the religion a religion upon whose soundness the prophets have agreed." I say: The intended meaning of this religion must be something distinct from the legal obligations and rulings, because these differ and vary. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a way﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 48].

﻿[p. 135]

Therefore the intended meaning must be those matters that do not differ with the difference of the laws: faith in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day. Faith necessitates turning away from this world, turning toward the Hereafter, striving for noble character, and guarding against base conditions. In my view, it is also permissible that the intended meaning of His saying ﴿and do not divide﴾ is: do not divide by taking many gods, just as Joseph (peace be upon him) said: ﴿Are separate lords better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?﴾ [Yusuf: 39]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25].

Some have argued from His saying ﴿He has ordained for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah﴾ that the Prophet (ﷺ) was, at the beginning of his mission, sent with the law of Noah (peace be upon him). Would that it occurred so that it would become clear to us that the truth is what we are upon, or what Muhammad and his companions are upon. To dispel this doubt, God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, but those who believe are apprehensive of it﴾. The meaning is clear. They are apprehensive and fearful only because they know that at its occurrence repentance is impossible; as for the denier of resurrection, it is so that this fear does not occur to him.

Then He said: ﴿Unquestionably, those who dispute about the Hour are in extreme error﴾. Al-mumara is persistent contention. Al-Zajjaj said: those into whom doubt and uncertainty about the occurrence of the Hour enter, so they dispute about it and deny it. ﴿Are in extreme error﴾ because the restoration of the oppressed person's right from the oppressor is obligatory in justice; so if the Resurrection did not occur, it would follow that injustice is attributed to God, exalted is He, and this is among the most absurd impossibilities; therefore denying the Resurrection is indeed extreme error.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿God is Subtle with His servants﴾, i.e., abundantly beneficent toward them. The mention of this statement here is appropriate because He revealed to them the Book containing these subtle proofs, so that was among God's subtle kindness to His servants. Also, those who disbelieved deserved severe punishment, yet God deferred that punishment from them, and that too is among God's subtle kindness. Since the bringing of the greatest benefits to them and the warding off of the greatest harms from them had been mentioned, it is therefore fitting that it be mentioned here. Then He said: ﴿He provides for whom He wills﴾, meaning that the root of beneficence and goodness is general with respect to all servants, and that is beneficence through life, reason, and understanding, and the granting of what is indispensable of provision, and the warding off of most calamities and afflictions from them. As for the degrees of bounty and delight, they vary and differ.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And He is the Strong﴾, i.e., the Able over everything He wills, ﴿the Mighty﴾, who cannot be overcome or resisted.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 42, verses 13–19 (part 1 of 2):

﴿He has ordained for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and what We revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: that you establish the religion and do not divide over it. Hard for the polytheists is that to which you call them. Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance.﴾ ﴿And they did not divide except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord for a specified term, the matter would have been decided between them. And indeed, those who were given the Scripture after them are in disquieting doubt concerning it.﴾ ﴿So for that, invite, and remain steadfast as you were commanded, and do not follow their desires. And say: "I believe in whatever Allah has sent down of Scripture, and I was commanded to act justly between you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. There is no argument between us and you. Allah will bring us together, and to Him is the final return."﴾ ﴿And those who argue about Allah after He has been responded to, their argument is baseless with their Lord, and upon them is anger, and for them is a severe punishment.﴾ ﴿It is Allah who has sent down the Book in truth, and the balance. And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.﴾ ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe fear it and know that it is the truth. Unquestionably, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in far error.﴾ ﴿Allah is Subtle with His servants; He provides for whom He wills, and He is the Strong, the Mighty.﴾

Know that when He, the Exalted, magnified His revelation to Muhammad (ﷺ) by His saying: ﴿Thus He reveals to you, and to those before you, Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [al-Shura: 3], He then mentioned in this verse the detail of that. He said: ﴿He has ordained for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah.﴾ The meaning is: He has ordained for you, O companions of Muhammad, of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah, Muhammad, Abraham, Moses and Jesus. This is the intended meaning of the wording of the verse. He specifically mentioned these five prophets because they are the greatest of the prophets, the possessors of the great laws and the numerous followers. However, there remain difficulties in the wording of the verse.

The first: He said at the beginning of the verse ﴿what He enjoined upon Noah﴾, and at its end ﴿and what We enjoined upon Abraham﴾, and in the middle ﴿and what We revealed to you﴾. So what is the benefit of this variation?

The second: He mentioned Noah (peace be upon him) in the third person, saying ﴿what He enjoined upon Noah﴾, while the other two parts are in the first person plural, saying ﴿and what We revealed to you and what We enjoined upon Abraham﴾.

The third: The sense of the verse becomes: "Allah has ordained for you of the religion that which We revealed to you." So His saying ﴿He has ordained for you﴾ is addressed in the third person, while His saying ﴿what We revealed to you﴾ is addressed in the second person. This requires combining address in the third person and address in the second person in a single utterance under a single consideration, and this is problematic. These difficulties must be investigated, and the people [i.e., the commentators] have not revolved around them.

In sum, the purpose of the verse is that it is said: "He has ordained for you of the religion a religion upon whose soundness the prophets have agreed." I say: The intended meaning of this religion must be something distinct from the legal obligations and rulings, because these differ and vary. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a way﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 48].

﻿[p. 135]

Therefore the intended meaning must be those matters that do not differ with the difference of the laws: faith in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day. Faith necessitates turning away from this world, turning toward the Hereafter, striving for noble character, and guarding against base conditions. In my view, it is also permissible that the intended meaning of His saying ﴿and do not divide﴾ is: do not divide by taking many gods, just as Joseph (peace be upon him) said: ﴿Are separate lords better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?﴾ [Yusuf: 39]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25].

Some have argued from His saying ﴿He has ordained for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah﴾ that the Prophet (ﷺ) was, at the beginning of his mission, sent with the law of Noah (peace be upon him). The answer is what we have mentioned: He joined all the other prophets to it by the conjunction, and this indicates that the intended meaning is adherence to the law agreed upon by all.

The grammatical position of ﴿that establish the religion﴾ is either an accusative in apposition to the object of ﴿ordained﴾ and the two items conjoined to it, or a nominative by resumption, as if it were said: "What is that which was ordained?" It was answered: "It is the establishment of the religion."

﴿Hard for the polytheists is﴾: it was great and burdensome for them ﴿that to which you call them﴾, namely the establishment of the religion of Allah, the Exalted, in the manner of agreement and consensus. The evidence for this is that the disbelievers said: ﴿Has he made the gods into one god? Indeed, this is an astonishing thing!﴾ [Sad: 5]. Here there are several issues:

The first issue: Those who deny analogical reasoning (qiyas) have argued from this verse. They said: He, the Exalted, informed us that the greatest of the prophets agreed that it is obligatory to establish the religion in a manner that does not lead to disagreement and dispute. Allah, the Exalted, mentioned, as a favor upon His servants, that He guided them to a religion free of division and opposition. It is known that opening the door to qiyas leads to the greatest kinds of division and contention. Experience bears witness that those who built their religion on the adoption of qiyas have divided into a division with no hope of agreement among them until the Day of Resurrection. Therefore it must be prohibited and forbidden.

The second issue: This verse indicates that these laws are of two kinds:

One kind is that to which the introduction of abrogation (naskh) and change is impossible; rather it remains obligatory in all laws and religions, such as the view that truthfulness, justice and benevolence are good, and the view that lying, injustice and harming others are ugly.

The other kind is that which differs with the difference of laws and religions. This verse indicates that the legislator's effort to establish the first kind is stronger than his effort to establish the second kind, because persistence in the first kind is important for acquiring the states that bring about happiness in the Hereafter.

The third issue: His, the Exalted, saying ﴿that you establish the religion and do not divide over it﴾ indicates that attaining agreement is a demanded matter in both the Law and reason. The explanation of its benefit is in several aspects:

The first: Souls have influences, and when souls agree and concur upon one thing, the influence becomes strong.

The second: When they concur, each one of them becomes a helper to the other in that specific aim, and the multiplicity of helpers brings about the attainment of the aim. But when they differ, they dispute and argue, and so they weaken, and the aim is not attained.

The third: The occurrence of dispute is contrary to the interest of the world, because it leads to chaos (al-harj wa-al-maraj), killing and plunder. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, commanded in this verse the establishment of the religion in a way that does not lead to division, and He said in another verse: ﴿And do not dispute, lest you lose courage﴾ [al-Anfal: 46].

* * *

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance﴾. There are two interpretations of this:

The first: When He, the Exalted, guided the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) to adhering to the religion agreed upon, He made clear that He guided them to this good only because He chose them, selected them, and singled them out with abundant mercy and honor.

The second: The call of the messengers was burdensome for them only because of the submission it required to them out of arrogance and pride. So He, the Exalted, made clear that He singles out whom He wills with the messengership, and submission to them is obligatory. Lineage, ancestry and wealth are not taken into account; rather all are equal in that they are obligated to follow the messengers whom Allah, the Exalted, has chosen. The derivation of the word "ijtiba'" (choosing) indicates gathering and collecting, from which comes "jaba al-kharaj" (he collected the tax) and "jaba al-ma'a fi al-hawd" (he gathered the water into the basin). So His saying ﴿Allah chooses for Himself﴾ means He gathers him to Himself and brings him close with the nearness of honor and mercy. His saying ﴿whom He wills﴾ is like His saying: ﴿He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills﴾ [al-Ankabut: 21].

* * *

Then He said: ﴿and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance﴾. This is, as has been related in the report: "Whoever draws near to Me a handspan, I draw near to him an arm's length; and whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running." That is: whoever turns toward Him with obedience, He turns toward him with His guidance and direction, by expanding his breast and facilitating his affair.

Know that when He, the Exalted, made clear that He commanded all the prophets and nations to adhere to the religion agreed upon, someone could say: "Then why do we find them divided?" So Allah, the Exalted, answered on their behalf by His saying: ﴿And they did not divide except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves.﴾ He means: they did not divide except after they knew that division is misguidance; but they did so out of envy and the pursuit of leadership. Natural zeal and innate pride drove each group to adopt a doctrine, call people to it, and disparage whatever else was other than it, seeking fame and leadership. This became the cause of the occurrence of disagreement. Then He, the Exalted, informed us that they deserved punishment because of this act. However, He, the Exalted, delayed that punishment from them, because for every punishment with Him there is a specified term, that is, a known time, either for the sheer exercise of His will, as is our position, or because He knew that the good lies in its realization at that time, as the Mu'tazilah hold. This is the meaning of His saying ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord for a specified term, the matter would have been decided between them.﴾ The specified term may be in this world or in the Resurrection. The commentators differed about those who are meant by this description. Most said: They are the Jews and the Christians. The evidence is His saying in Al 'Imran: ﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves﴾ [Al 'Imran: 19], and His saying in the surah "Lam yakun": ﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not divide except after the clear evidence had come to them﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 4]. Also, His saying ﴿except after knowledge had come to them﴾ is fitting for the People of the Book.

Others said: They are the Arabs. This is false, for the reasons mentioned. His saying, the Exalted, after this verse ﴿And indeed, those who were given the Scripture after them﴾ does not befit the Arabs, because "those who were given the Scripture after them" are the People of the Book who were in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ﴿are in disquieting doubt concerning it﴾, concerning their own Book, ﴿disquieting﴾, not believing in it with true faith.

* * *

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So for that, invite, and remain steadfast as you were commanded﴾. That is: for the sake of that division, and for the sake of the many disagreements that arose in the religion, invite people to agreement upon the upright monotheistic faith (al-millah al-hanifiyyah), remain steadfast upon it and upon calling to it as Allah commanded you, and do not follow their divergent, false desires. ﴿And say: "I believe in whatever Allah has sent down of Scripture"﴾, that is, in whatever Scripture it is established that Allah sent down. That means belief in all the revealed books, because those who divided believed in some and disbelieved in others. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿We believe in some and disbelieve in others﴾ [al-Nisa': 150], up to His saying ﴿those are the disbelievers in truth﴾ [al-Nisa': 151]. Then He said: ﴿And I was commanded to act justly between you﴾, that is, in judgment, when you dispute and bring your disputes to me for judgment. Al-Qaffal said: its meaning is that my Lord commanded me not to distinguish between myself and yourselves, by commanding you to do what I do not do, or by opposing you in what I have forbidden you; rather I treat you equally with myself. Likewise I treat your great ones and your small ones equally in matters that concern the judgment of Allah.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. There is no argument between us and you. Allah will bring us together, and to Him is the final return.﴾

[p. 137]

The meaning is that the God of all is one, and each person is specifically responsible for his own deeds. Therefore each person must occupy himself in this world with his own self, for God will gather all of them together on the Day of Resurrection and recompense each one for his deeds. The intended purpose of this is disengagement (al-mutarakah) and each person's occupation with his own important matters. If it is said: how does what was done to them of killing, destruction of their houses, cutting down of palm trees, and expulsion befit this disengagement? We say: this disengagement was conditional upon their accepting the religion whose soundness is agreed upon among all the prophets, which includes monotheism (al-tawhid), abandoning the worship of idols, affirming the prophethood of the prophets, and affirming the truth of the resurrection and the Last Day. When they did not accept this religion, the condition was then unfulfilled, and therefore the conditioned matter was unfulfilled.

* * *

Know that the intended meaning of His words ﴿There is no argument between us and you﴾ is not the prohibition of what is similar to their disputation. Several points show this:

First: this statement is mentioned in the context of disputation. If the intended meaning of this verse were the prohibition of disputation, it would follow that it is prohibited in itself, and this is contradictory.

Second: were it not for the proofs, obligation would not have been directed.

Third: proof produces knowledge, and that cannot be prohibited. Rather, the intended meaning is that the people recognized by the proof the truth of Muhammad (ﷺ), and they only abandoned affirming him out of rebellion and obstinacy. So God, exalted is He, made clear that the need to dispute with them has been eliminated, because they have recognized his truth through the proof; so there is no need whatsoever to dispute with them. Among what strengthens our view that disputation cannot be prohibited is His words ﴿And argue with them in the best manner﴾ [al-Nahl: 125], His words ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in the best manner﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 46], His words ﴿O Noah, you have disputed with us and multiplied our disputation﴾ [Hud: 32], and His words ﴿And that was Our argument which We gave to Abraham against his people﴾ [al-An'am: 83].

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who argue about God﴾, i.e., dispute concerning His religion, ﴿after it has been responded to﴾, i.e., after people have responded to that religion, ﴿their argument is baseless﴾, i.e., false. That dispute was that the Jews said: Do you not say that adhering to what is agreed upon is better than adhering to what is disputed? The prophethood of Moses and the truth of the Torah are known by consensus, while the prophethood of Muhammad is not agreed upon. So if you build your speech in this verse on the premise that adhering to what is agreed upon is better, then it must be that Judaism is better to adhere to. God, exalted is He, then made clear that this argument is baseless, i.e., false and corrupt. That is because the Jews agreed that faith in Moses, peace be upon him, was obligatory only because of the manifestation of miracles in accordance with his claim, and here miracles manifested in accordance with the claim of Muhammad, peace be upon him, and the Jews witnessed those miracles. If the manifestation of a miracle indicates truthfulness, then here it is obligatory to acknowledge the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ); and if it does not indicate truthfulness, then it would be obligatory regarding Moses that they not acknowledge his prophethood. As for acknowledging the prophethood of Moses while persisting in denying the prophethood of Muhammad, despite both being equal in the manifestation of miracles, this is contradictory.

Perhaps the Hour is near﴾. So His saying ﴿Allah chooses for Himself﴾ means He gathers him to Himself and brings him close with the nearness of honor and mercy. His saying ﴿whom He wills﴾ is like His saying: ﴿He punishes whom He wills and has mercy on whom He wills﴾ [al-Ankabut: 21].

* * *

Then He said: ﴿and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance﴾. This is, as has been related in the report: "Whoever draws near to Me a handspan, I draw near to him an arm's length; and whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running." That is: whoever turns toward Him with obedience, He turns toward him with His guidance and direction, by expanding his breast and facilitating his affair.

Know that when He, the Exalted, made clear that He commanded all the prophets and nations to adhere to the religion agreed upon, someone could say: "Then why do we find them divided?" So Allah, the Exalted, answered on their behalf by His saying: ﴿And they did not divide except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves.﴾ He means: they did not divide except after they knew that division is misguidance; but they did so out of envy and the pursuit of leadership. Natural zeal and innate pride drove each group to adopt a doctrine, call people to it, and disparage whatever else was other than it, seeking fame and leadership. This became the cause of the occurrence of disagreement. Then He, the Exalted, informed us that they deserved punishment because of this act. However, He, the Exalted, delayed that punishment from them, because for every punishment with Him there is a specified term, that is, a known time, either for the sheer exercise of His will, as is our position, or because He knew that the good lies in its realization at that time, as the Mu'tazilah hold. This is the meaning of His saying ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord for a specified term, the matter would have been decided between them.﴾ The specified term may be in this world or in the Resurrection. The commentators differed about those who are meant by this description. Most said: They are the Jews and the Christians. The evidence is His saying in Al 'Imran: ﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves﴾ [Al 'Imran: 19], and His saying in the surah "Lam yakun": ﴿And those who were given the Scripture did not divide except after the clear evidence had come to them﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 4]. Also, His saying ﴿except after knowledge had come to them﴾ is fitting for the People of the Book.

Others said: They are the Arabs. This is false, for the reasons mentioned. His saying, the Exalted, after this verse ﴿And indeed, those who were given the Scripture after them﴾ does not befit the Arabs, because "those who were given the Scripture after them" are the People of the Book who were in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), ﴿are in disquieting doubt concerning it﴾, concerning their own Book, ﴿disquieting﴾, not believing in it with true faith.

* * *

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So for that, invite, and remain steadfast as you were commanded﴾. That is: for the sake of that division, and for the sake of the many disagreements that arose in the religion, invite people to agreement upon the upright monotheistic faith (al-millah al-hanifiyyah), remain steadfast upon it and upon calling to it as Allah commanded you, and do not follow their divergent, false desires. ﴿And say: "I believe in whatever Allah has sent down of Scripture"﴾, that is, in whatever Scripture it is established that Allah sent down. That means belief in all the revealed books, because those who divided believed in some and disbelieved in others. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿We believe in some and disbelieve in others﴾ [al-Nisa': 150], up to His saying ﴿those are the disbelievers in truth﴾ [al-Nisa': 151]. Then He said: ﴿And I was commanded to act justly between you﴾, that is, in judgment, when you dispute and bring your disputes to me for judgment. Al-Qaffal said: its meaning is that my Lord commanded me not to distinguish between myself and yourselves, by commanding you to do what I do not do, or by opposing you in what I have forbidden you; rather I treat you equally with myself. Likewise I treat your great ones and your small ones equally in matters that concern the judgment of Allah.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. There is no argument between us and you. Allah will bring us together, and to Him is the final return.﴾

[p. 137]

The meaning is that the God of all is one, and each person is specifically responsible for his own deeds. Therefore each person must occupy himself in this world with his own self, for God will gather all of them together on the Day of Resurrection and recompense each one for his deeds. The intended purpose of this is disengagement (al-mutarakah) and each person's occupation with his own important matters. If it is said: how does what was done to them of killing, destruction of their houses, cutting down of palm trees, and expulsion befit this disengagement? We say: this disengagement was conditional upon their accepting the religion whose soundness is agreed upon among all the prophets, which includes monotheism (al-tawhid), abandoning the worship of idols, affirming the prophethood of the prophets, and affirming the truth of the resurrection and the Last Day. When they did not accept this religion, the condition was then unfulfilled, and therefore the conditioned matter was unfulfilled.

* * *

Know that the intended meaning of His words ﴿There is no argument between us and you﴾ is not the prohibition of what is similar to their disputation. Several points show this:

First: this statement is mentioned in the context of disputation. If the intended meaning of this verse were the prohibition of disputation, it would follow that it is prohibited in itself, and this is contradictory.

Second: were it not for the proofs, obligation would not have been directed.

Third: proof produces knowledge, and that cannot be prohibited. Rather, the intended meaning is that the people recognized by the proof the truth of Muhammad (ﷺ), and they only abandoned affirming him out of rebellion and obstinacy. So God, exalted is He, made clear that the need to dispute with them has been eliminated, because they have recognized his truth through the proof; so there is no need whatsoever to dispute with them. Among what strengthens our view that disputation cannot be prohibited is His words ﴿And argue with them in the best manner﴾ [al-Nahl: 125], His words ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in the best manner﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 46], His words ﴿O Noah, you have disputed with us and multiplied our disputation﴾ [Hud: 32], and His words ﴿And that was Our argument which We gave to Abraham against his people﴾ [al-An'am: 83].

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who argue about God﴾, i.e., dispute concerning His religion, ﴿after it has been responded to﴾, i.e., after people have responded to that religion, ﴿their argument is baseless﴾, i.e., false. That dispute was that the Jews said: Do you not say that adhering to what is agreed upon is better than adhering to what is disputed? The prophethood of Moses and the truth of the Torah are known by consensus, while the prophethood of Muhammad is not agreed upon. So if you build your speech in this verse on the premise that adhering to what is agreed upon is better, then it must be that Judaism is better to adhere to. God, exalted is He, then made clear that this argument is baseless, i.e., false and corrupt. That is because the Jews agreed that faith in Moses, peace be upon him, was obligatory only because of the manifestation of miracles in accordance with his claim, and here miracles manifested in accordance with the claim of Muhammad, peace be upon him, and the Jews witnessed those miracles. If the manifestation of a miracle indicates truthfulness, then here it is obligatory to acknowledge the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ); and if it does not indicate truthfulness, then it would be obligatory regarding Moses that they not acknowledge his prophethood. As for acknowledging the prophethood of Moses while persisting in denying the prophethood of Muhammad, despite both being equal in the manifestation of miracles, this is contradictory.

When God established these proofs, He warned the deniers with the punishment of the Resurrection, saying: ﴿It is God who revealed the Book with truth and the Balance. And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾. The meaning is: God, exalted is He, revealed the Book which contains various kinds of proofs and clear evidences, and revealed the Balance, which is the criterion that is the upright scale, and that they do not know when the Resurrection will suddenly come upon them. Since this is the case, it is obligatory for the rational person to strive and exert effort in reflection and reasoning, and to abandon the way of the people of ignorance and blind imitation. Since the Messenger was threatening them with the descent of the Resurrection and repeated this a great deal, and they saw no effect of it, they said in mockery: When will the Resurrection occur? Would that it occurred so that it would become clear to us that the truth is what we are upon, or what Muhammad and his companions are upon. To dispel this doubt, God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, but those who believe are apprehensive of it﴾. The meaning is clear. They are apprehensive and fearful only because they know that at its occurrence repentance is impossible; as for the denier of resurrection, it is so that this fear does not occur to him.

Then He said: ﴿Unquestionably, those who dispute about the Hour are in extreme error﴾. Al-mumara is persistent contention. Al-Zajjaj said: those into whom doubt and uncertainty about the occurrence of the Hour enter, so they dispute about it and deny it. ﴿Are in extreme error﴾ because the restoration of the oppressed person's right from the oppressor is obligatory in justice; so if the Resurrection did not occur, it would follow that injustice is attributed to God, exalted is He, and this is among the most absurd impossibilities; therefore denying the Resurrection is indeed extreme error.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿God is Subtle with His servants﴾, i.e., abundantly beneficent toward them. The mention of this statement here is appropriate because He revealed to them the Book containing these subtle proofs, so that was among God's subtle kindness to His servants. Also, those who disbelieved deserved severe punishment, yet God deferred that punishment from them, and that too is among God's subtle kindness. Since the bringing of the greatest benefits to them and the warding off of the greatest harms from them had been mentioned, it is therefore fitting that it be mentioned here. Then He said: ﴿He provides for whom He wills﴾, meaning that the root of beneficence and goodness is general with respect to all servants, and that is beneficence through life, reason, and understanding, and the granting of what is indispensable of provision, and the warding off of most calamities and afflictions from them. As for the degrees of bounty and delight, they vary and differ.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And He is the Strong﴾, i.e., the Able over everything He wills, ﴿the Mighty﴾, who cannot be overcome or resisted.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 42, verses 13–19 (part 1 of 2):

﴿He has ordained for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and what We revealed to you, and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: that you establish the religion and do not divide over it. Hard for the polytheists is that to which you call them. Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance.﴾ ﴿And they did not divide except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord for a specified term, the matter would have been decided between them. And indeed, those who were given the Scripture after them are in disquieting doubt concerning it.﴾ ﴿So for that, invite, and remain steadfast as you were commanded, and do not follow their desires. And say: "I believe in whatever Allah has sent down of Scripture, and I was commanded to act justly between you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. There is no argument between us and you. Allah will bring us together, and to Him is the final return."﴾ ﴿And those who argue about Allah after He has been responded to, their argument is baseless with their Lord, and upon them is anger, and for them is a severe punishment.﴾ ﴿It is Allah who has sent down the Book in truth, and the balance. And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near.﴾ ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe fear it and know that it is the truth. Unquestionably, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in far error.﴾ ﴿Allah is Subtle with His servants; He provides for whom He wills, and He is the Strong, the Mighty.﴾

Know that when He, the Exalted, magnified His revelation to Muhammad (ﷺ) by His saying: ﴿Thus He reveals to you, and to those before you, Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [al-Shura: 3], He then mentioned in this verse the detail of that. He said: ﴿He has ordained for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah.﴾ The meaning is: He has ordained for you, O companions of Muhammad, of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah, Muhammad, Abraham, Moses and Jesus. This is the intended meaning of the wording of the verse. He specifically mentioned these five prophets because they are the greatest of the prophets, the possessors of the great laws and the numerous followers. However, there remain difficulties in the wording of the verse.

The first: He said at the beginning of the verse ﴿what He enjoined upon Noah﴾, and at its end ﴿and what We enjoined upon Abraham﴾, and in the middle ﴿and what We revealed to you﴾. So what is the benefit of this variation?

The second: He mentioned Noah (peace be upon him) in the third person, saying ﴿what He enjoined upon Noah﴾, while the other two parts are in the first person plural, saying ﴿and what We revealed to you and what We enjoined upon Abraham﴾.

The third: The sense of the verse becomes: "Allah has ordained for you of the religion that which We revealed to you." So His saying ﴿He has ordained for you﴾ is addressed in the third person, while His saying ﴿what We revealed to you﴾ is addressed in the second person. This requires combining address in the third person and address in the second person in a single utterance under a single consideration, and this is problematic. These difficulties must be investigated, and the people [i.e., the commentators] have not revolved around them.

In sum, the purpose of the verse is that it is said: "He has ordained for you of the religion a religion upon whose soundness the prophets have agreed." I say: The intended meaning of this religion must be something distinct from the legal obligations and rulings, because these differ and vary. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a way﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 48].

﻿[p. 135]

Therefore the intended meaning must be those matters that do not differ with the difference of the laws: faith in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day. Faith necessitates turning away from this world, turning toward the Hereafter, striving for noble character, and guarding against base conditions. In my view, it is also permissible that the intended meaning of His saying ﴿and do not divide﴾ is: do not divide by taking many gods, just as Joseph (peace be upon him) said: ﴿Are separate lords better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer?﴾ [Yusuf: 39]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25].

Some have argued from His saying ﴿He has ordained for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah﴾ that the Prophet (ﷺ) was, at the beginning of his mission, sent with the law of Noah (peace be upon him). The answer is what we have mentioned: He joined all the other prophets to it by the conjunction, and this indicates that the intended meaning is adherence to the law agreed upon by all.

The grammatical position of ﴿that establish the religion﴾ is either an accusative in apposition to the object of ﴿ordained﴾ and the two items conjoined to it, or a nominative by resumption, as if it were said: "What is that which was ordained?" It was answered: "It is the establishment of the religion."

﴿Hard for the polytheists is﴾: it was great and burdensome for them ﴿that to which you call them﴾, namely the establishment of the religion of Allah, the Exalted, in the manner of agreement and consensus. The evidence for this is that the disbelievers said: ﴿Has he made the gods into one god? Indeed, this is an astonishing thing!﴾ [Sad: 5]. Here there are several issues:

The first issue: Those who deny analogical reasoning (qiyas) have argued from this verse. They said: He, the Exalted, informed us that the greatest of the prophets agreed that it is obligatory to establish the religion in a manner that does not lead to disagreement and dispute. Allah, the Exalted, mentioned, as a favor upon His servants, that He guided them to a religion free of division and opposition. It is known that opening the door to qiyas leads to the greatest kinds of division and contention. Experience bears witness that those who built their religion on the adoption of qiyas have divided into a division with no hope of agreement among them until the Day of Resurrection. Therefore it must be prohibited and forbidden.

The second issue: This verse indicates that these laws are of two kinds:

One kind is that to which the introduction of abrogation (naskh) and change is impossible; rather it remains obligatory in all laws and religions, such as the view that truthfulness, justice and benevolence are good, and the view that lying, injustice and harming others are ugly.

The other kind is that which differs with the difference of laws and religions. This verse indicates that the legislator's effort to establish the first kind is stronger than his effort to establish the second kind, because persistence in the first kind is important for acquiring the states that bring about happiness in the Hereafter.

The third issue: His, the Exalted, saying ﴿that you establish the religion and do not divide over it﴾ indicates that attaining agreement is a demanded matter in both the Law and reason. The explanation of its benefit is in several aspects:

The first: Souls have influences, and when souls agree and concur upon one thing, the influence becomes strong.

The second: When they concur, each one of them becomes a helper to the other in that specific aim, and the multiplicity of helpers brings about the attainment of the aim. But when they differ, they dispute and argue, and so they weaken, and the aim is not attained.

The third: The occurrence of dispute is contrary to the interest of the world, because it leads to chaos (al-harj wa-al-maraj), killing and plunder. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, commanded in this verse the establishment of the religion in a way that does not lead to division, and He said in another verse: ﴿And do not dispute, lest you lose courage﴾ [al-Anfal: 46].

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And He is the Strong﴾, i.e., the Able over everything He wills, ﴿the Mighty﴾, who cannot be overcome or resisted.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 42, verse 20–26 (part 1 of 3):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We shall increase for him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We shall give him of it, but he will have no share in the Hereafter.﴾ ﴿Or do they have partners who have instituted for them in religion what Allah has not permitted? And were it not for the decisive word, they would have been judged between. And indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.﴾ ﴿You will see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned, while it is going to befall them. But those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the gardens of Paradise; they will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty.﴾ ﴿That is what Allah gives good tidings of to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds. Say, "I do not ask you for it any reward except affection for relatives." And whoever commits a good deed - We increase for him therein good. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾ ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented about Allah a lie"? But if Allah willed, He would seal your heart. And Allah eliminates falsehood and establishes the truth by His words. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.﴾ ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds and knows what you do.﴾ ﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds and gives them increase from His bounty. But the disbelievers will have a severe punishment.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, explained that He is Subtle with His servants and abundant in beneficence toward them, He explained that they must strive in seeking good things and in guarding against vile deeds. So He said: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We shall increase for him in his tilth.﴾ The author of al-Kashshaf (al-Kashshaf, the Qur'anic commentary of al-Zamakhshari) said: He, exalted is He, called what the doer does, by which he seeks benefit, "tilth" (ḥarth) by way of metaphor. In the verse there are issues:

The first issue: In this verse He, exalted is He, showed the distinction between one who desires the Hereafter and one who desires this world in several respects:

The first: He mentioned the one who desires the tilth of the Hereafter before the one who desires the tilth of this world, and this indicates preference, because He described it as "the Hereafter"; then He placed it first in mention as an alert to His saying, "We are the last [in time] but the first [in rank]."

The second: He said regarding the one who desires the tilth of the Hereafter, ﴿We shall increase for him in his tilth﴾, and regarding the one who desires the tilth of this world, ﴿We shall give him of it﴾. The word "min" (of) is for partitive meaning, so the sense is that He gives him part of what he seeks and does not give him all of it. And in Surat Bani Isra'il He said: ﴿We hasten to him therein what We will, for whom We intend﴾ [al-Isra' 17:18]. I say: rational proof supports both aspects, because whoever works for the Hereafter and persists in that work, the abundance of deeds is a cause for the attainment of dispositions (malakat). Thus whoever persists in those deeds more, his heart's inclination toward seeking the Hereafter is greater, and whenever this is so, joy is greater and felicities are more numerous; and that is what is meant by His saying, ﴿We shall increase for him in his tilth﴾. As for the seeker of this world, whenever his persistence in the works of that seeking is greater, his desire to attain this world is greater and his inclination toward it stronger; and when inclination is always increasing while the attainment of the sought thing remains in one state, deprivation is inevitably necessary.

The third: He, exalted is He, said regarding the seeker of the tilth of the Hereafter, ﴿We shall increase for him in his tilth﴾, and did not mention whether He gives him this world or not, but the speech remained silent about it, affirmatively and negatively. As for the seeker of the tilth of this world, He explicitly stated that He does not give him any share of the Hereafter. This indicates a great disparity; as if He were saying: the Hereafter is the root and this world is the branch, so one who finds the root will find the branch to the extent of need. However, He did not mention that, as an alert that this world is too base to have its mention paired with the mention of the Hereafter.

The fourth: He, exalted is He, explained that the seeker of the Hereafter has his sought thing increased, and explained that the seeker of this world is given some of his sought thing from this world, but in the Hereafter he has absolutely no share. Thus by the first statement He showed that the state of the seeker of the Hereafter is always in ascent and increase, and by the second statement He showed that the state of the seeker of this world, in the first station, is in decline, and in the second station, in complete nullity.

The fifth: The Hereafter is credit (nasi'ah) and this world is cash (naqd), and credit is deemed inferior relative to cash, since people say: cash is better than credit. So He, exalted is He, showed that this judgment is reversed with respect to the states of the Hereafter and this world. The Hereafter, although it is credit, is oriented toward increase and permanence, so it is better and more perfect; and this world, although it is cash, is oriented toward decline and then toward nullity, so it is baser and more abject. This indicates that the state of the Hereafter does not at all resemble the state of this world, and that there is in this world of the states of the Hereafter nothing but the mere name, as is related from Ibn ʿAbbas.

The sixth: The verse indicates that the benefits of the Hereafter and this world are not immediately present; rather, in both realms tilth is necessary, and tilth cannot be accomplished except by bearing hardships in sowing, then watering, nurturing, harvesting, and then cleaning. So when God named both kinds "tilth," we knew that each of them is attained only by bearing toils and hardships. Then He explained that the outcome of the Hereafter is toward increase and perfection, and that the outcome of this world is toward decline and then annihilation. So it is as if it were said: if both kinds necessarily require bearing the toils of tilling, watering, nurturing, harvesting and cleaning, then it is more fitting that these toils be directed toward what is in increase and permanence than toward what is in decline, cessation and annihilation.

The second issue: Regarding His saying, ﴿We shall increase for him in his tilth﴾, there are two opinions:

The first: The meaning is that We increase in his success, his aid, and the facilitation of the paths of good deeds and acts of obedience for him. Muqatil said: ﴿We shall increase for him in his tilth﴾ by multiplying the reward. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿That He may pay them their rewards and increase them from His bounty﴾ [Fatir 35:30]. And it is related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Whoever rises in the morning with the concern of this world, Allah scatters his concern and places his poverty before his eyes, and what has not been written for him of this world does not come to him; and whoever rises in the morning with the concern of the Hereafter, Allah gathers his concern and places his richness in his heart, and this world comes to him while it is humbled." Or a wording close to this meaning.

The third issue: The apparent wording indicates that whoever prays for the sake of seeking reward or for the sake of averting punishment, his prayer is valid; but they have agreed that it is not valid. The answer: God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter﴾, and tilth cannot be achieved except by casting the correct seed into the earth, and the correct seed for all good things and felicities is nothing but the worship of Allah, exalted is He.

The fourth issue: Our companions said: if one performs ablution without intention, it is not valid. They said: because this person did not desire the tilth of the Hereafter, since the discussion concerns one who is heedless of the remembrance of Allah and of the Hereafter; therefore he must not obtain a share in what relates to the Hereafter, and discharging the obligation of prayer belongs to the category of the benefits of the Hereafter, so it must not be attained in ablution devoid of intention.

Know that when God, exalted is He, explained the greatest law and the most upright balance in the works of the Hereafter and this world, He followed it with an alert to what is fundamental in the domain of error and misery, so He said: ﴿Or do they have partners who have instituted for them in religion what Allah has not permitted?﴾ The meaning of the interrogative hamza in "am" is affirmation and rebuke. "Their partners" (shuraka'uhum) are their devils who adorned polytheism, the denial of resurrection, and working for this world, since they know nothing other than it. It was said: "their partners" are their idols; and they were attributed to them because they are the ones who took them as partners to Allah. And since they were the cause of their misguidance, they were made to legislate the religion of error, as Abraham ﷺ said: ﴿My Lord, they have led astray many of the people﴾ [Ibrahim 14:36]. And His saying, ﴿They have instituted for them in religion what Allah has not permitted﴾ means that all those laws are in opposition to Allah. Then He said: ﴿And were it not for the decisive word﴾, i.e., the prior decree to delay the recompense, or it is said: were it not for the promise that the decisive judgment would be on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿they would have been judged between them﴾, i.e., between the disbelievers and the believers, or between the polytheists and their partners. ﴿And indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.﴾ Some read "wa-anna" with the hamza of "inna" opened, as a conjunction to "the decisive word," meaning: ﴿were it not for the decisive word﴾ and that their being punished in the Hereafter ﴿they would have been judged between them﴾ in this world. Then He, exalted is He, mentioned the states of the people of punishment and the states of the people of reward.

As for the first: it is His saying, ﴿You will see the wrongdoers fearful﴾, fearing intensely, ﴿of what they have earned﴾ of misdeeds, ﴿while it is going to befall them﴾; He means that its consequence is going to befall them, whether they feared or did not fear.

As for the second: it is the states of the people of reward, and it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the gardens of Paradise﴾, because the garden of Paradise is the most pleasant spot in it. In the verse there is an alert that all the sinful people of the prayer are in Paradise, except that He specified those who believed and did righteous deeds for the gardens of Paradise, which are the noble spots of Paradise; so the spots below those gardens must necessarily be specified for those who were below those who believed and did righteous deeds. Then He said: ﴿They will have whatever they wish with their Lord﴾

This indicates that all things are present with Him, prepared. Then God, exalted is He, said in magnifying this rank: ﴿That is the great bounty.﴾ Our companions have used this verse to argue that reward is not obligatory upon Allah, but occurs by way of bounty from Allah, exalted is He. He said: ﴿Those who believed and did righteous deeds in the gardens of Paradise will have whatever they wish with their Lord﴾; this indicates that the gardens of Paradise and finding everything they desire is a recompense for faith and righteous deeds.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿That is the great bounty.﴾ This is an explicit statement that the recompense attached to deeds occurred by way of bounty, not by way of entitlement.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿That is what Allah gives good tidings of to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds.﴾ The author of al-Kashshaf said: it is read "yubashshiru" from "bashsharahu," "yubshiru" from "absharahu," and "yabshuru" from "bashara."

Know that these verses indicate the magnification of the state of reward in several respects:

The first: that Allah, glorified is He, attached to faith and righteous deeds the gardens of Paradise. A sovereign who is the greatest of beings and the most generous, when he attaches a recompense to arduous deeds, that indicates that this recompense has reached a point whose true nature none knows but Allah, exalted is He.

The second: He, exalted is He, said: ﴿They will have whatever they wish with their Lord﴾, and His saying ﴿They will have whatever they wish﴾ falls within the category of the infinite, because there is no rank except that a person desires what is higher than it.

The third: He, exalted is He, said: ﴿That is the great bounty﴾, and the one whose greatness is judged by He who has absolute majesty and grandeur is in utmost greatness.

The fourth: He, exalted is He, repeated the good tidings as a form of magnification, saying: ﴿That which Allah gives good tidings of to His servants﴾, and that also indicates the utmost grandeur. We ask Allah for success in them and for arrival at them.

Know that when He, exalted is He, revealed to Muhammad ﷺ this noble and exalted Book, and deposited in it the three categories: proofs, kinds of obligations, and attached reward to obedience and punishment to disobedience, He explained: I do not ask you, by means of this conveyance, for any immediate benefit or present gain, lest an ignorant person imagine that Muhammad's ﷺ purpose from this conveyance is wealth or status. So He said: ﴿Say, "I do not ask you for it any reward except affection for relatives."﴾ And in this there are issues:

The first issue: People have mentioned three opinions regarding this verse:

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 42, verses 20–26 (part 2 of 3):

First: al-Sha'bi said: "People argued with us about this verse, so we wrote to Ibn 'Abbas asking him about it. Ibn 'Abbas wrote that the Messenger of God ﷺ was the central point of lineage among the Quraysh, there being no clan (batn) of theirs to which he was not related by birth. So God said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward﴾ for what I call you to, ﴿except﴾ that you show love to me because of my kinship with you.
