The meaning is: 'You are my people, and you are the most deserving of those who should respond to me and obey me. Since you have refused this, then at least preserve the right of kinship, do not harm me, and do not stir up opposition against me.'"

The second view: al-Kalbi narrated, "from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina, he was afflicted with calamities and obligations, and he had no means at his disposal. The Ansar said: 'This man has been guided by God through his hand, he is the son of your sister, and your neighbour in your city. So gather for him a portion of your wealth.' They did so, then brought it to him, but he returned it to them. Then the words of God, exalted is He, were revealed: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it﴾, that is, for faith, ﴿except that you love my relatives﴾. So He urged them to love his relatives."

[p. 142]

The third view: what al-Hasan mentioned, he said: "except that you show love (tawaddud) to God, through what brings you closer to Him, namely drawing near to Him through righteous deeds." So the word "al-qurba" (kinship) in the first view means blood-relationship (rahim), in the second it means the relatives themselves, and in the third it is a form (fu'la) from nearness (qurb) and bringing near (taqrib).

If it is said: the verse is problematic, because seeking a reward for conveying revelation is not permissible, and this is shown by several considerations:

First: God related of most of the prophets, peace be upon them, that they explicitly denied seeking any wage. He mentioned in the story of Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿And I ask you no reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 109]. Likewise in the stories of Hud and Salih, and in the stories of Lut and Shu'ayb, peace be upon them all. Our Prophet is more excellent than all the other prophets, peace be upon them, so it is more fitting that he should not seek a reward for prophethood and messengership.

Second: He ﷺ explicitly denied seeking a reward in other verses. He said: ﴿Say: whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours﴾ [Saba: 47], and he said: ﴿Say: I ask you no reward for it, and I am not one of the pretenders﴾ [Sad: 86].

Third: reason also indicates this, because that conveying was obligatory upon him. God said: ﴿Convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67]. And seeking a reward for performing an obligation is not fitting even for the least of people, let alone the most learned of scholars.

Fourth: prophethood is more excellent than wisdom (hikmah). God said of wisdom: ﴿And whoever is given wisdom has indeed been given much good﴾ [al-Baqarah: 269], and said of the worldly life: ﴿Say: the enjoyment of this world is little﴾ [al-Nisa: 77]. So how can it be reasonable to set the most noble of things against the basest of things?

Fifth: seeking a reward would give rise to suspicion, and that contradicts certainty in the soundness of prophethood.

By these considerations it is established that it is not permissible for the Prophet ﷺ to seek any reward at all for conveying and messengership. The apparent meaning of this verse, however, requires that he sought a reward for conveying and messengership, namely love in kinship. This is the statement of the objection. As for the answer: there is no dispute that it is not permissible to seek a reward for conveying and messengership. What remains is His words ﴿except love in kinship﴾. We say that the answer to it is in two ways:

The first: this is of the type of the poet's saying:

"There is no fault in them, except that their swords bear the notches of the armoured men's blows."

The meaning: "I ask nothing from you except this." But in reality this is not a reward, because the existence of love among Muslims is an obligation. God said: ﴿And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another﴾ [al-Tawbah: 71]. And he ﷺ said: "The believers are like a building, each part strengthening the others." The verses and reports on this theme are numerous. If the existence of love among the majority of Muslims is obligatory, then its existence toward the most noble and eminent of Muslims is more fitting. His words: ﴿Say: I ask you no reward for it, except love in kinship﴾, mean: "Love in kinship is not a reward," so the result returns to the conclusion that there is no reward at all.

The second answer: this is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati'), and the speech is complete at His words ﴿Say: I ask you no reward for it﴾. Then He said: ﴿except love in kinship﴾, meaning: "But I remind you of my kinship with you," and it appears in wording as a reward, but it is not a reward.

Third issue: the author of al-Kashshaf transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad dies as a martyr. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad dies forgiven. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad dies repentant. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad dies a believer whose faith is complete. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad, the Angel of Death gives him the good news of Paradise, then Munkar and Nakir. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad is escorted to Paradise as a bride is escorted to her husband's house. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad, two doors to Paradise are opened for him in his grave. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad,"

[p. 143]

"God makes his grave a place of visitation for the angels of mercy. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad dies upon the Sunnah and the Community. Oh, and whoever dies upon hatred of the family of Muhammad comes on the Day of Resurrection with 'despairing of God's mercy' written between his eyes. Oh, and whoever dies upon hatred of the family of Muhammad dies a disbeliever. Oh, and whoever dies upon hatred of the family of Muhammad will not smell the fragrance of Paradise." This is what the author of al-Kashshaf transmitted. As for me, I say: the family of Muhammad ﷺ are those whose affairs return to him. Whoever's affairs were most strongly and perfectly connected to him, those are the family (al-al). There is no doubt that Fatimah, 'Ali, al-Hasan and al-Husayn had the strongest connection with the Messenger of God ﷺ, and this is known by mass-transmitted (mutawatir) report. Therefore they must be the family. Also, people differed about the meaning of "al" (family). It was said: they are the kinsmen. It was said: they are his community. If we take it to mean kinsmen, then they are the family. If we take it to mean the community who accepted his call, then they too are family. So it is established that under all interpretations they are the family. As for others, whether they enter under the term "al", this is disputed.

The author of al-Kashshaf also transmitted that when this verse was revealed, "it was said: O Messenger of God, who are these relatives of yours whose love has become obligatory upon us? He said: 'Ali, Fatimah, and their two sons.'" Thus it is established that these four are relatives of the Prophet ﷺ, and when this is established, they must be singled out for greater honour. This is shown by several considerations:

First: His words ﴿except love in kinship﴾, and the way of deducing from it is what has preceded.

Second: There is no doubt that the Prophet ﷺ loved Fatimah, upon her be peace. He ﷺ said: "Fatimah is a part of me; whatever hurts her hurts me." And it is established by mass-transmitted report from the Messenger of God ﷺ that he loved 'Ali, al-Hasan and al-Husayn. If this is established, then it is obligatory upon the whole community to do likewise, by His words: ﴿Follow him, that you may be guided﴾ [al-A'raf: 158], and by His words: ﴿Let those who oppose his command beware﴾, and by His words: ﴿Say: if you love God, then follow me, and God will love you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 31], and by His words, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed there is for you in the Messenger of God an excellent example﴾ [al-Ahzab: 21].

Third: invoking blessings upon the family is a great station, and for this reason this supplication was made the closing part of the tashahhud in prayer, namely: "O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, and have mercy upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad." This honour has not been found for anyone other than the family. All of this shows that love for the family of Muhammad is obligatory. Al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him, said:

"O rider, halt at al-Muhassab in Mina, and call out to the one who dwells in its valley and the one who rises up,
at dawn when the pilgrims pour out toward Mina, in a flow like the overflowing of the Euphrates,
If loving the family of Muhammad is rafd (rejection), then let both jinn and men bear witness that I am a rafidi."

The fourth issue: His words ﴿except love in kinship﴾ contain a great station for the Companions, because He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost, those are the ones brought near﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 10–11]. So everyone who obeyed God was brought near to God, exalted is He, and therefore enters under His words ﴿except love in kinship﴾. The conclusion: this verse indicates the obligation of loving the family of the Messenger of God ﷺ and loving his Companions. This station is not secure except according to our companions, the people of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah), who combined love for the progeny (al-'itrah) and love for the Companions. I heard some of those mentioned say that he ﷺ said: "The likeness of my family is like the ark of Noah: whoever boarded it was saved." He ﷺ also said: "My Companions are like the stars; whichever of them you follow, you will be guided." We are now in the sea of obligation, and the waves of doubts and desires strike us, and the one who rides the sea needs two things:

One of them: a ship free of defects and holes.

The second: bright, shining stars that rise. When he boards that ship and his gaze falls upon those shining stars, the hope of safety becomes strong. Likewise, our companions, the people of the Sunnah, boarded the ship of love for the family of Muhammad, and fixed their gaze upon the stars of the Companions, so they hope from God, exalted is He, to attain safety and happiness in this world and the Hereafter.

* * *

[p. 144]

Let us return to the exegesis. The author of al-Kashshaf raised an objection against himself, saying: "Why was it not said: 'except love for kinship' or 'except love for the relatives'? And what is the meaning of His words ﴿except love in kinship﴾?" He answered it by saying: "They made (the kinship) a place for the love and a seat for it, as in the saying: 'I have love for the family of so-and-so, and I have affection and intense love for them,' meaning: 'I love them, and they are the place and locus of my love.'"

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever earns a good deed, We increase for him good therein﴾. It was said: this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him. The apparent meaning is general, for whatever good deed it may be. However, since it is mentioned right after the mention of love in kinship, this indicates that the intention is to emphasise that love.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed God is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾. The word "Shakur" (Appreciative), when applied to God, exalted is He, is metaphorical. The meaning is that He, exalted is He, does good to the obedient by bringing reward to them, and by adding to it many kinds of favour.

God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against God"?﴾ Know that the discourse at the beginning of the surah was started to establish that this Book came through the revelation of God, which is His words, exalted is He: ﴿Thus does God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise, reveal to you and to those before you﴾ [al-Shura: 3]. The discourse continued in establishing this meaning, and some parts were connected to others, until it reached this point. Then He related here the doubt of the people, which is their saying that this is not a revelation from God, exalted is He. So He said: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against God"?﴾

The author of al-Kashshaf said: "Am" (or) is disconnected (munqati'ah), and the meaning of the interrogative hamzah is itself rebuke; it is as if it were said: 'Does it occur to their hearts and pass on their tongues that they should attribute the like of this to fabrication against God, which is the worst and most shameful kind of slander?' Then he answered it by saying: ﴿If God wills, He would seal over your heart﴾. In this there are several views:

First: Mujahid said: "He would bind your heart with patience in bearing their harm, so that their saying 'he is a fabricator, a liar' does not grieve you."

Second: The meaning of this statement is that if God willed, He would make you among those whose hearts are sealed, so that you would fabricate lies against Him. For no one dares to fabricate lies against God except one who is in such a state. The purpose of mentioning this statement is to emphasise the strong improbability (istib'ad). An example of this is that a man accuses one of the trustworthy of treachery, and the trustworthy one says: "Perhaps God has forsaken me; perhaps God has blinded my heart." He does not intend to affirm forsaking or blindness of heart in himself, but only to make the emergence of treachery from him seem highly unlikely.

* * *

And then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah effaces falsehood and establishes truth by His words﴾. That is: it is part of Allah's custom to nullify falsehood and confirm truth. So if Muhammad were a liar and a fabricator, Allah would have exposed him and revealed his falsehood, and He would not have supported him with strength and victory. Since this is not the case, we know that he is not among the liars who fabricate against Allah. It is also possible that this is a promise from Allah to His Messenger that He will efface the falsehood they hold to, namely their slander, calumny and denial, and establish the truth upon which Muhammad ﷺ stood.
* * *
Then He said: ﴿Indeed, He is Knower of what is within the breasts﴾. That is: Allah knows what is in your breast and in theirs, and matters proceed according to that. It is related from Qatadah: "If He wills, He would seal your heart, causing you to forget the Qur'an and cutting off revelation from you," meaning: if he had fabricated a lie against Allah, Allah would have done that to him.

Know that when He, Exalted, said: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated against Allah a lie"?﴾, then He cleared His Messenger of what they attributed to him in this regard, and it was known that they deserved a great punishment for this slander. Therefore Allah urged them to repent and informed them that He accepts it from every wrongdoer, however great his wrong, so He said: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds﴾. In this verse there are several issues:

Issue one: The author of al-Kashshaf said: It is said "qabiltu minhu al-shay'" and "qabiltuhu 'anhu." The meaning of "qabiltuhu minhu" is that I took it from him and made him the origin and source of acceptance. The meaning of "qabiltuhu 'anhu" is that I took it and established it on his behalf. The thorough discussion of the reality of repentance has already preceded in Surat al-Baqarah. The least that is indispensable is regret for the past, abandoning the sin in the present, and resolving not to return to it in the future. Jabir narrated that a Bedouin entered the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Allah, I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You," and he said the takbir. When he finished his prayer, 'Ali (peace be upon him) said to him: "O man, quickness of the tongue in seeking forgiveness is the repentance of liars; your repentance needs repentance." He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, what is repentance?" He said: "It is a term that applies to six things: for past sins, regret; for neglecting obligations, making them up; restoring usurped rights; melting the self in obedience just as you raised it in disobedience; making the self taste the bitterness of obedience just as you made it taste the sweetness of disobedience; and weeping in place of every laugh you laughed."

Issue two: The Mu'tazilah said: it is obligatory upon Allah, by reason, to accept repentance. Our companions said: nothing is obligatory upon Allah; whatever He does, He does out of generosity and grace. They argued for the soundness of their position with this verse, saying: He, Exalted, praised Himself by accepting repentance, and if that acceptance were obligatory, the great praise would not have occurred. Do you not see that if someone praises himself by saying he does not strike people unjustly or kill them in anger, that is only minor praise; but if he says, "I do good to them, although that is not obligatory upon me," that is praise and commendation?

Issue three: His saying, Exalted: ﴿and pardons misdeeds﴾ — either it means that He pardons major sins after the coming of repentance, or it means that He pardons minor sins, or it means that He pardons major sins before repentance. The first is invalid, for otherwise His saying ﴿and pardons misdeeds﴾ would be the same as His saying ﴿it is He who accepts repentance﴾, and repetition is contrary to the basic principle. The second is also invalid, because that is obligatory, and performing an obligation is not a ground for praise. So the third part remains, and the meaning is: sometimes He pardons through the medium of accepting repentance, and sometimes He pardons directly without repentance.
* * *
Then He said: ﴿and He knows what you do﴾. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs from 'Asim read it with the ta' (second person, addressing), while the rest read it with the ya' (third person, absent). The meaning: Allah knows it, so He rewards him for his good deeds and punishes him for his misdeeds.
* * *
Then He said: ﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds and increases them from His bounty﴾. In this there are two views:

One: "Those who believe and do righteous deeds" is in the nominative as the subject; its implied sense is: the believers respond to Allah in what He has called them to.

The second: its position is accusative, and the subject is a hidden pronoun, which is Allah; its implied sense is: Allah responds to the believers, except that the lam was omitted, as it was omitted in His saying ﴿and when they measure for them﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 3]. This second view is preferable, because the report before and after it is about Allah: what precedes the verse is His saying ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds﴾, and what follows it is His saying ﴿and increases them from His bounty﴾. So "yazid" is conjoined to "yastajib." According to the first view: the servant responds, and Allah increases from His bounty.

As for those who say the verb belongs to the believers, there are two views:
One: the believers respond to their Lord in what He has called them to.
The second: they obey Him in what He has commanded them, and istijabah is obedience.

As for those who say the verb belongs to Allah, they have differed. It is said: Allah responds to the supplication of the believers and increases them in what they asked of His bounty. If they say: does singling out the believers for the answering of supplication indicate that He, Exalted, does not answer the supplication of the disbelievers? We say: some of them said: it is not permissible, because answering supplication is an honour, and that is not fitting for disbelievers. It was also said: it is permissible in some respects, and the benefit of the specification is that the answering of the believers' supplication is by way of honour, while the answering of the disbelievers' supplication is by way of gradual respite. Then He said: ﴿and increases them from His bounty﴾, that is: He increases them beyond what they asked for in supplication. ﴿And for the disbelievers is a severe punishment﴾, and the purpose is warning.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 42, verse 20–26 (part 1 of 3):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We shall increase for him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We shall give him of it, but he will have no share in the Hereafter.﴾ ﴿Or do they have partners who have instituted for them in religion what Allah has not permitted? And were it not for the decisive word, they would have been judged between. And indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.﴾ ﴿You will see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned, while it is going to befall them. But those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the gardens of Paradise; they will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty.﴾ ﴿That is what Allah gives good tidings of to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds. Say, "I do not ask you for it any reward except affection for relatives." And whoever commits a good deed - We increase for him therein good. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾ ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented about Allah a lie"? But if Allah willed, He would seal your heart. And Allah eliminates falsehood and establishes the truth by His words. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.﴾ ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds and knows what you do.﴾ ﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds and gives them increase from His bounty. But the disbelievers will have a severe punishment.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, explained that He is Subtle with His servants and abundant in beneficence toward them, He explained that they must strive in seeking good things and in guarding against vile deeds. So He said: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We shall increase for him in his tilth.﴾ The author of al-Kashshaf (al-Kashshaf, the Qur'anic commentary of al-Zamakhshari) said: He, exalted is He, called what the doer does, by which he seeks benefit, "tilth" (ḥarth) by way of metaphor. In the verse there are issues:

The first issue: In this verse He, exalted is He, showed the distinction between one who desires the Hereafter and one who desires this world in several respects:

The first: He mentioned the one who desires the tilth of the Hereafter before the one who desires the tilth of this world, and this indicates preference, because He described it as "the Hereafter"; then He placed it first in mention as an alert to His saying, "We are the last [in time] but the first [in rank]."

The second: He said regarding the one who desires the tilth of the Hereafter, ﴿We shall increase for him in his tilth﴾, and regarding the one who desires the tilth of this world, ﴿We shall give him of it﴾. The word "min" (of) is for partitive meaning, so the sense is that He gives him part of what he seeks and does not give him all of it. And in Surat Bani Isra'il He said: ﴿We hasten to him therein what We will, for whom We intend﴾ [al-Isra' 17:18]. I say: rational proof supports both aspects, because whoever works for the Hereafter and persists in that work, the abundance of deeds is a cause for the attainment of dispositions (malakat). Thus whoever persists in those deeds more, his heart's inclination toward seeking the Hereafter is greater, and whenever this is so, joy is greater and felicities are more numerous; and that is what is meant by His saying, ﴿We shall increase for him in his tilth﴾. As for the seeker of this world, whenever his persistence in the works of that seeking is greater, his desire to attain this world is greater and his inclination toward it stronger; and when inclination is always increasing while the attainment of the sought thing remains in one state, deprivation is inevitably necessary.

The third: He, exalted is He, said regarding the seeker of the tilth of the Hereafter, ﴿We shall increase for him in his tilth﴾, and did not mention whether He gives him this world or not, but the speech remained silent about it, affirmatively and negatively. As for the seeker of the tilth of this world, He explicitly stated that He does not give him any share of the Hereafter. This indicates a great disparity; as if He were saying: the Hereafter is the root and this world is the branch, so one who finds the root will find the branch to the extent of need. However, He did not mention that, as an alert that this world is too base to have its mention paired with the mention of the Hereafter.

The fourth: He, exalted is He, explained that the seeker of the Hereafter has his sought thing increased, and explained that the seeker of this world is given some of his sought thing from this world, but in the Hereafter he has absolutely no share. Thus by the first statement He showed that the state of the seeker of the Hereafter is always in ascent and increase, and by the second statement He showed that the state of the seeker of this world, in the first station, is in decline, and in the second station, in complete nullity.

The fifth: The Hereafter is credit (nasi'ah) and this world is cash (naqd), and credit is deemed inferior relative to cash, since people say: cash is better than credit. So He, exalted is He, showed that this judgment is reversed with respect to the states of the Hereafter and this world. The Hereafter, although it is credit, is oriented toward increase and permanence, so it is better and more perfect; and this world, although it is cash, is oriented toward decline and then toward nullity, so it is baser and more abject. This indicates that the state of the Hereafter does not at all resemble the state of this world, and that there is in this world of the states of the Hereafter nothing but the mere name, as is related from Ibn ʿAbbas.

The sixth: The verse indicates that the benefits of the Hereafter and this world are not immediately present; rather, in both realms tilth is necessary, and tilth cannot be accomplished except by bearing hardships in sowing, then watering, nurturing, harvesting, and then cleaning. So when God named both kinds "tilth," we knew that each of them is attained only by bearing toils and hardships. Then He explained that the outcome of the Hereafter is toward increase and perfection, and that the outcome of this world is toward decline and then annihilation. So it is as if it were said: if both kinds necessarily require bearing the toils of tilling, watering, nurturing, harvesting and cleaning, then it is more fitting that these toils be directed toward what is in increase and permanence than toward what is in decline, cessation and annihilation.

The second issue: Regarding His saying, ﴿We shall increase for him in his tilth﴾, there are two opinions:

The first: The meaning is that We increase in his success, his aid, and the facilitation of the paths of good deeds and acts of obedience for him. Muqatil said: ﴿We shall increase for him in his tilth﴾ by multiplying the reward. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿That He may pay them their rewards and increase them from His bounty﴾ [Fatir 35:30]. And it is related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Whoever rises in the morning with the concern of this world, Allah scatters his concern and places his poverty before his eyes, and what has not been written for him of this world does not come to him; and whoever rises in the morning with the concern of the Hereafter, Allah gathers his concern and places his richness in his heart, and this world comes to him while it is humbled." Or a wording close to this meaning.

The third issue: The apparent wording indicates that whoever prays for the sake of seeking reward or for the sake of averting punishment, his prayer is valid; but they have agreed that it is not valid. The answer: God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter﴾, and tilth cannot be achieved except by casting the correct seed into the earth, and the correct seed for all good things and felicities is nothing but the worship of Allah, exalted is He.

The fourth issue: Our companions said: if one performs ablution without intention, it is not valid. They said: because this person did not desire the tilth of the Hereafter, since the discussion concerns one who is heedless of the remembrance of Allah and of the Hereafter; therefore he must not obtain a share in what relates to the Hereafter, and discharging the obligation of prayer belongs to the category of the benefits of the Hereafter, so it must not be attained in ablution devoid of intention.

Know that when God, exalted is He, explained the greatest law and the most upright balance in the works of the Hereafter and this world, He followed it with an alert to what is fundamental in the domain of error and misery, so He said: ﴿Or do they have partners who have instituted for them in religion what Allah has not permitted?﴾ The meaning of the interrogative hamza in "am" is affirmation and rebuke. "Their partners" (shuraka'uhum) are their devils who adorned polytheism, the denial of resurrection, and working for this world, since they know nothing other than it. It was said: "their partners" are their idols; and they were attributed to them because they are the ones who took them as partners to Allah. And since they were the cause of their misguidance, they were made to legislate the religion of error, as Abraham ﷺ said: ﴿My Lord, they have led astray many of the people﴾ [Ibrahim 14:36]. And His saying, ﴿They have instituted for them in religion what Allah has not permitted﴾ means that all those laws are in opposition to Allah. Then He said: ﴿And were it not for the decisive word﴾, i.e., the prior decree to delay the recompense, or it is said: were it not for the promise that the decisive judgment would be on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿they would have been judged between them﴾, i.e., between the disbelievers and the believers, or between the polytheists and their partners. ﴿And indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.﴾ Some read "wa-anna" with the hamza of "inna" opened, as a conjunction to "the decisive word," meaning: ﴿were it not for the decisive word﴾ and that their being punished in the Hereafter ﴿they would have been judged between them﴾ in this world. Then He, exalted is He, mentioned the states of the people of punishment and the states of the people of reward.

As for the first: it is His saying, ﴿You will see the wrongdoers fearful﴾, fearing intensely, ﴿of what they have earned﴾ of misdeeds, ﴿while it is going to befall them﴾; He means that its consequence is going to befall them, whether they feared or did not fear.

As for the second: it is the states of the people of reward, and it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the gardens of Paradise﴾, because the garden of Paradise is the most pleasant spot in it. In the verse there is an alert that all the sinful people of the prayer are in Paradise, except that He specified those who believed and did righteous deeds for the gardens of Paradise, which are the noble spots of Paradise; so the spots below those gardens must necessarily be specified for those who were below those who believed and did righteous deeds. Then He said: ﴿They will have whatever they wish with their Lord﴾

This indicates that all things are present with Him, prepared. Then God, exalted is He, said in magnifying this rank: ﴿That is the great bounty.﴾ Our companions have used this verse to argue that reward is not obligatory upon Allah, but occurs by way of bounty from Allah, exalted is He. He said: ﴿Those who believed and did righteous deeds in the gardens of Paradise will have whatever they wish with their Lord﴾; this indicates that the gardens of Paradise and finding everything they desire is a recompense for faith and righteous deeds.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿That is the great bounty.﴾ This is an explicit statement that the recompense attached to deeds occurred by way of bounty, not by way of entitlement.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿That is what Allah gives good tidings of to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds.﴾ The author of al-Kashshaf said: it is read "yubashshiru" from "bashsharahu," "yubshiru" from "absharahu," and "yabshuru" from "bashara."

Know that these verses indicate the magnification of the state of reward in several respects:

The first: that Allah, glorified is He, attached to faith and righteous deeds the gardens of Paradise. A sovereign who is the greatest of beings and the most generous, when he attaches a recompense to arduous deeds, that indicates that this recompense has reached a point whose true nature none knows but Allah, exalted is He.

The second: He, exalted is He, said: ﴿They will have whatever they wish with their Lord﴾, and His saying ﴿They will have whatever they wish﴾ falls within the category of the infinite, because there is no rank except that a person desires what is higher than it.

The third: He, exalted is He, said: ﴿That is the great bounty﴾, and the one whose greatness is judged by He who has absolute majesty and grandeur is in utmost greatness.

The fourth: He, exalted is He, repeated the good tidings as a form of magnification, saying: ﴿That which Allah gives good tidings of to His servants﴾, and that also indicates the utmost grandeur. We ask Allah for success in them and for arrival at them.

Know that when He, exalted is He, revealed to Muhammad ﷺ this noble and exalted Book, and deposited in it the three categories: proofs, kinds of obligations, and attached reward to obedience and punishment to disobedience, He explained: I do not ask you, by means of this conveyance, for any immediate benefit or present gain, lest an ignorant person imagine that Muhammad's ﷺ purpose from this conveyance is wealth or status. So He said: ﴿Say, "I do not ask you for it any reward except affection for relatives."﴾ And in this there are issues:

The first issue: People have mentioned three opinions regarding this verse:

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 42, verses 20–26 (part 2 of 3):

First: al-Sha'bi said: "People argued with us about this verse, so we wrote to Ibn 'Abbas asking him about it. Ibn 'Abbas wrote that the Messenger of God ﷺ was the central point of lineage among the Quraysh, there being no clan (batn) of theirs to which he was not related by birth. So God said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward﴾ for what I call you to, ﴿except﴾ that you show love to me because of my kinship with you. The meaning is: 'You are my people, and you are the most deserving of those who should respond to me and obey me. Since you have refused this, then at least preserve the right of kinship, do not harm me, and do not stir up opposition against me.'"

The second view: al-Kalbi narrated, "from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina, he was afflicted with calamities and obligations, and he had no means at his disposal. The Ansar said: 'This man has been guided by God through his hand, he is the son of your sister, and your neighbour in your city. So gather for him a portion of your wealth.' They did so, then brought it to him, but he returned it to them. Then the words of God, exalted is He, were revealed: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it﴾, that is, for faith, ﴿except that you love my relatives﴾. So He urged them to love his relatives."

[p. 142]

The third view: what al-Hasan mentioned, he said: "except that you show love (tawaddud) to God, through what brings you closer to Him, namely drawing near to Him through righteous deeds." So the word "al-qurba" (kinship) in the first view means blood-relationship (rahim), in the second it means the relatives themselves, and in the third it is a form (fu'la) from nearness (qurb) and bringing near (taqrib).

If it is said: the verse is problematic, because seeking a reward for conveying revelation is not permissible, and this is shown by several considerations:

First: God related of most of the prophets, peace be upon them, that they explicitly denied seeking any wage. He mentioned in the story of Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿And I ask you no reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 109]. Likewise in the stories of Hud and Salih, and in the stories of Lut and Shu'ayb, peace be upon them all. Our Prophet is more excellent than all the other prophets, peace be upon them, so it is more fitting that he should not seek a reward for prophethood and messengership.

Second: He ﷺ explicitly denied seeking a reward in other verses. He said: ﴿Say: whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours﴾ [Saba: 47], and he said: ﴿Say: I ask you no reward for it, and I am not one of the pretenders﴾ [Sad: 86].

Third: reason also indicates this, because that conveying was obligatory upon him. God said: ﴿Convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67]. And seeking a reward for performing an obligation is not fitting even for the least of people, let alone the most learned of scholars.

Fourth: prophethood is more excellent than wisdom (hikmah). God said of wisdom: ﴿And whoever is given wisdom has indeed been given much good﴾ [al-Baqarah: 269], and said of the worldly life: ﴿Say: the enjoyment of this world is little﴾ [al-Nisa: 77]. So how can it be reasonable to set the most noble of things against the basest of things?

Fifth: seeking a reward would give rise to suspicion, and that contradicts certainty in the soundness of prophethood.

By these considerations it is established that it is not permissible for the Prophet ﷺ to seek any reward at all for conveying and messengership. The apparent meaning of this verse, however, requires that he sought a reward for conveying and messengership, namely love in kinship. This is the statement of the objection. As for the answer: there is no dispute that it is not permissible to seek a reward for conveying and messengership. What remains is His words ﴿except love in kinship﴾. We say that the answer to it is in two ways:

The first: this is of the type of the poet's saying:

"There is no fault in them, except that their swords bear the notches of the armoured men's blows."

The meaning: "I ask nothing from you except this." But in reality this is not a reward, because the existence of love among Muslims is an obligation. God said: ﴿And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another﴾ [al-Tawbah: 71]. And he ﷺ said: "The believers are like a building, each part strengthening the others." The verses and reports on this theme are numerous. If the existence of love among the majority of Muslims is obligatory, then its existence toward the most noble and eminent of Muslims is more fitting. His words: ﴿Say: I ask you no reward for it, except love in kinship﴾, mean: "Love in kinship is not a reward," so the result returns to the conclusion that there is no reward at all.

The second answer: this is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati'), and the speech is complete at His words ﴿Say: I ask you no reward for it﴾. Then He said: ﴿except love in kinship﴾, meaning: "But I remind you of my kinship with you," and it appears in wording as a reward, but it is not a reward.

Third issue: the author of al-Kashshaf transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad dies as a martyr. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad dies forgiven. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad dies repentant. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad dies a believer whose faith is complete. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad, the Angel of Death gives him the good news of Paradise, then Munkar and Nakir. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad is escorted to Paradise as a bride is escorted to her husband's house. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad, two doors to Paradise are opened for him in his grave. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad,"

[p. 143]

"God makes his grave a place of visitation for the angels of mercy. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad dies upon the Sunnah and the Community. Oh, and whoever dies upon hatred of the family of Muhammad comes on the Day of Resurrection with 'despairing of God's mercy' written between his eyes. Oh, and whoever dies upon hatred of the family of Muhammad dies a disbeliever. Oh, and whoever dies upon hatred of the family of Muhammad will not smell the fragrance of Paradise." This is what the author of al-Kashshaf transmitted. As for me, I say: the family of Muhammad ﷺ are those whose affairs return to him. Whoever's affairs were most strongly and perfectly connected to him, those are the family (al-al). There is no doubt that Fatimah, 'Ali, al-Hasan and al-Husayn had the strongest connection with the Messenger of God ﷺ, and this is known by mass-transmitted (mutawatir) report. Therefore they must be the family. Also, people differed about the meaning of "al" (family). It was said: they are the kinsmen. It was said: they are his community. If we take it to mean kinsmen, then they are the family. If we take it to mean the community who accepted his call, then they too are family. So it is established that under all interpretations they are the family. As for others, whether they enter under the term "al", this is disputed.

The author of al-Kashshaf also transmitted that when this verse was revealed, "it was said: O Messenger of God, who are these relatives of yours whose love has become obligatory upon us? He said: 'Ali, Fatimah, and their two sons.'" Thus it is established that these four are relatives of the Prophet ﷺ, and when this is established, they must be singled out for greater honour. This is shown by several considerations:

First: His words ﴿except love in kinship﴾, and the way of deducing from it is what has preceded.

Second: There is no doubt that the Prophet ﷺ loved Fatimah, upon her be peace. He ﷺ said: "Fatimah is a part of me; whatever hurts her hurts me." And it is established by mass-transmitted report from the Messenger of God ﷺ that he loved 'Ali, al-Hasan and al-Husayn. If this is established, then it is obligatory upon the whole community to do likewise, by His words: ﴿Follow him, that you may be guided﴾ [al-A'raf: 158], and by His words: ﴿Let those who oppose his command beware﴾, and by His words: ﴿Say: if you love God, then follow me, and God will love you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 31], and by His words, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed there is for you in the Messenger of God an excellent example﴾ [al-Ahzab: 21].

Third: invoking blessings upon the family is a great station, and for this reason this supplication was made the closing part of the tashahhud in prayer, namely: "O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, and have mercy upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad." This honour has not been found for anyone other than the family. All of this shows that love for the family of Muhammad is obligatory. Al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him, said:

"O rider, halt at al-Muhassab in Mina, and call out to the one who dwells in its valley and the one who rises up,
at dawn when the pilgrims pour out toward Mina, in a flow like the overflowing of the Euphrates,
If loving the family of Muhammad is rafd (rejection), then let both jinn and men bear witness that I am a rafidi."

The fourth issue: His words ﴿except love in kinship﴾ contain a great station for the Companions, because He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost, those are the ones brought near﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 10–11]. So everyone who obeyed God was brought near to God, exalted is He, and therefore enters under His words ﴿except love in kinship﴾. The conclusion: this verse indicates the obligation of loving the family of the Messenger of God ﷺ and loving his Companions. This station is not secure except according to our companions, the people of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah), who combined love for the progeny (al-'itrah) and love for the Companions. I heard some of those mentioned say that he ﷺ said: "The likeness of my family is like the ark of Noah: whoever boarded it was saved." He ﷺ also said: "My Companions are like the stars; whichever of them you follow, you will be guided." We are now in the sea of obligation, and the waves of doubts and desires strike us, and the one who rides the sea needs two things:

One of them: a ship free of defects and holes.

The second: bright, shining stars that rise. When he boards that ship and his gaze falls upon those shining stars, the hope of safety becomes strong. Likewise, our companions, the people of the Sunnah, boarded the ship of love for the family of Muhammad, and fixed their gaze upon the stars of the Companions, so they hope from God, exalted is He, to attain safety and happiness in this world and the Hereafter.

* * *

[p. 144]

Let us return to the exegesis. The author of al-Kashshaf raised an objection against himself, saying: "Why was it not said: 'except love for kinship' or 'except love for the relatives'? And what is the meaning of His words ﴿except love in kinship﴾?" He answered it by saying: "They made (the kinship) a place for the love and a seat for it, as in the saying: 'I have love for the family of so-and-so, and I have affection and intense love for them,' meaning: 'I love them, and they are the place and locus of my love.'"

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever earns a good deed, We increase for him good therein﴾. It was said: this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him. The apparent meaning is general, for whatever good deed it may be. However, since it is mentioned right after the mention of love in kinship, this indicates that the intention is to emphasise that love.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed God is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾. The word "Shakur" (Appreciative), when applied to God, exalted is He, is metaphorical. The meaning is that He, exalted is He, does good to the obedient by bringing reward to them, and by adding to it many kinds of favour.

God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against God"?﴾ Know that the discourse at the beginning of the surah was started to establish that this Book came through the revelation of God, which is His words, exalted is He: ﴿Thus does God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise, reveal to you and to those before you﴾ [al-Shura: 3]. The discourse continued in establishing this meaning, and some parts were connected to others, until it reached this point. Then He related here the doubt of the people, which is their saying that this is not a revelation from God, exalted is He. So He said: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented a lie against God"?﴾

The author of al-Kashshaf said: "Am" (or) is disconnected (munqati'ah), and the meaning of the interrogative hamzah is itself rebuke; it is as if it were said: 'Does it occur to their hearts and pass on their tongues that they should attribute the like of this to fabrication against God, which is the worst and most shameful kind of slander?' Then he answered it by saying: ﴿If God wills, He would seal over your heart﴾. In this there are several views:

First: Mujahid said: "He would bind your heart with patience in bearing their harm, so that their saying 'he is a fabricator, a liar' does not grieve you."

Second: The meaning of this statement is that if God willed, He would make you among those whose hearts are sealed, so that you would fabricate lies against Him. For no one dares to fabricate lies against God except one who is in such a state. The purpose of mentioning this statement is to emphasise the strong improbability (istib'ad). An example of this is that a man accuses one of the trustworthy of treachery, and the trustworthy one says: "Perhaps God has forsaken me; perhaps God has blinded my heart." He does not intend to affirm forsaking or blindness of heart in himself, but only to make the emergence of treachery from him seem highly unlikely.

* * *

And then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah effaces falsehood and establishes truth by His words﴾. That is: it is part of Allah's custom to nullify falsehood and confirm truth. So if Muhammad were a liar and a fabricator, Allah would have exposed him and revealed his falsehood, and He would not have supported him with strength and victory. Since this is not the case, we know that he is not among the liars who fabricate against Allah. It is also possible that this is a promise from Allah to His Messenger that He will efface the falsehood they hold to, namely their slander, calumny and denial, and establish the truth upon which Muhammad ﷺ stood.
* * *
Then He said: ﴿Indeed, He is Knower of what is within the breasts﴾. That is: Allah knows what is in your breast and in theirs, and matters proceed according to that. It is related from Qatadah: "If He wills, He would seal your heart, causing you to forget the Qur'an and cutting off revelation from you," meaning: if he had fabricated a lie against Allah, Allah would have done that to him.

Know that when He, Exalted, said: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated against Allah a lie"?﴾, then He cleared His Messenger of what they attributed to him in this regard, and it was known that they deserved a great punishment for this slander. Therefore Allah urged them to repent and informed them that He accepts it from every wrongdoer, however great his wrong, so He said: ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds﴾. In this verse there are several issues:

Issue one: The author of al-Kashshaf said: It is said "qabiltu minhu al-shay'" and "qabiltuhu 'anhu." The meaning of "qabiltuhu minhu" is that I took it from him and made him the origin and source of acceptance. The meaning of "qabiltuhu 'anhu" is that I took it and established it on his behalf. The thorough discussion of the reality of repentance has already preceded in Surat al-Baqarah. The least that is indispensable is regret for the past, abandoning the sin in the present, and resolving not to return to it in the future. Jabir narrated that a Bedouin entered the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Allah, I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You," and he said the takbir. When he finished his prayer, 'Ali (peace be upon him) said to him: "O man, quickness of the tongue in seeking forgiveness is the repentance of liars; your repentance needs repentance." He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, what is repentance?" He said: "It is a term that applies to six things: for past sins, regret; for neglecting obligations, making them up; restoring usurped rights; melting the self in obedience just as you raised it in disobedience; making the self taste the bitterness of obedience just as you made it taste the sweetness of disobedience; and weeping in place of every laugh you laughed."

Issue two: The Mu'tazilah said: it is obligatory upon Allah, by reason, to accept repentance. Our companions said: nothing is obligatory upon Allah; whatever He does, He does out of generosity and grace. They argued for the soundness of their position with this verse, saying: He, Exalted, praised Himself by accepting repentance, and if that acceptance were obligatory, the great praise would not have occurred. Do you not see that if someone praises himself by saying he does not strike people unjustly or kill them in anger, that is only minor praise; but if he says, "I do good to them, although that is not obligatory upon me," that is praise and commendation?

Issue three: His saying, Exalted: ﴿and pardons misdeeds﴾ — either it means that He pardons major sins after the coming of repentance, or it means that He pardons minor sins, or it means that He pardons major sins before repentance. The first is invalid, for otherwise His saying ﴿and pardons misdeeds﴾ would be the same as His saying ﴿it is He who accepts repentance﴾, and repetition is contrary to the basic principle. The second is also invalid, because that is obligatory, and performing an obligation is not a ground for praise. So the third part remains, and the meaning is: sometimes He pardons through the medium of accepting repentance, and sometimes He pardons directly without repentance.
* * *
Then He said: ﴿and He knows what you do﴾. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs from 'Asim read it with the ta' (second person, addressing), while the rest read it with the ya' (third person, absent). The meaning: Allah knows it, so He rewards him for his good deeds and punishes him for his misdeeds.
* * *
Then He said: ﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds and increases them from His bounty﴾. In this there are two views:

One: "Those who believe and do righteous deeds" is in the nominative as the subject; its implied sense is: the believers respond to Allah in what He has called them to.

The second: its position is accusative, and the subject is a hidden pronoun, which is Allah; its implied sense is: Allah responds to the believers, except that the lam was omitted, as it was omitted in His saying ﴿and when they measure for them﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 3]. This second view is preferable, because the report before and after it is about Allah: what precedes the verse is His saying ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds﴾, and what follows it is His saying ﴿and increases them from His bounty﴾. So "yazid" is conjoined to "yastajib." According to the first view: the servant responds, and Allah increases from His bounty.

As for those who say the verb belongs to the believers, there are two views:
One: the believers respond to their Lord in what He has called them to.
The second: they obey Him in what He has commanded them, and istijabah is obedience.

As for those who say the verb belongs to Allah, they have differed. It is said: Allah responds to the supplication of the believers and increases them in what they asked of His bounty. If they say: does singling out the believers for the answering of supplication indicate that He, Exalted, does not answer the supplication of the disbelievers? We say: some of them said: it is not permissible, because answering supplication is an honour, and that is not fitting for disbelievers. It was also said: it is permissible in some respects, and the benefit of the specification is that the answering of the believers' supplication is by way of honour, while the answering of the disbelievers' supplication is by way of gradual respite. Then He said: ﴿and increases them from His bounty﴾, that is: He increases them beyond what they asked for in supplication. ﴿And for the disbelievers is a severe punishment﴾, and the purpose is warning.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 42, verse 20–26 (part 1 of 3):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We shall increase for him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We shall give him of it, but he will have no share in the Hereafter.﴾ ﴿Or do they have partners who have instituted for them in religion what Allah has not permitted? And were it not for the decisive word, they would have been judged between. And indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.﴾ ﴿You will see the wrongdoers fearful of what they have earned, while it is going to befall them. But those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the gardens of Paradise; they will have whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty.﴾ ﴿That is what Allah gives good tidings of to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds. Say, "I do not ask you for it any reward except affection for relatives." And whoever commits a good deed - We increase for him therein good. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Appreciative.﴾ ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented about Allah a lie"? But if Allah willed, He would seal your heart. And Allah eliminates falsehood and establishes the truth by His words. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.﴾ ﴿And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds and knows what you do.﴾ ﴿And He responds to those who believe and do righteous deeds and gives them increase from His bounty. But the disbelievers will have a severe punishment.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, explained that He is Subtle with His servants and abundant in beneficence toward them, He explained that they must strive in seeking good things and in guarding against vile deeds. So He said: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We shall increase for him in his tilth.﴾ The author of al-Kashshaf (al-Kashshaf, the Qur'anic commentary of al-Zamakhshari) said: He, exalted is He, called what the doer does, by which he seeks benefit, "tilth" (ḥarth) by way of metaphor. In the verse there are issues:

The first issue: In this verse He, exalted is He, showed the distinction between one who desires the Hereafter and one who desires this world in several respects:

The first: He mentioned the one who desires the tilth of the Hereafter before the one who desires the tilth of this world, and this indicates preference, because He described it as "the Hereafter"; then He placed it first in mention as an alert to His saying, "We are the last [in time] but the first [in rank]."

The second: He said regarding the one who desires the tilth of the Hereafter, ﴿We shall increase for him in his tilth﴾, and regarding the one who desires the tilth of this world, ﴿We shall give him of it﴾. The word "min" (of) is for partitive meaning, so the sense is that He gives him part of what he seeks and does not give him all of it. And in Surat Bani Isra'il He said: ﴿We hasten to him therein what We will, for whom We intend﴾ [al-Isra' 17:18]. I say: rational proof supports both aspects, because whoever works for the Hereafter and persists in that work, the abundance of deeds is a cause for the attainment of dispositions (malakat). Thus whoever persists in those deeds more, his heart's inclination toward seeking the Hereafter is greater, and whenever this is so, joy is greater and felicities are more numerous; and that is what is meant by His saying, ﴿We shall increase for him in his tilth﴾. As for the seeker of this world, whenever his persistence in the works of that seeking is greater, his desire to attain this world is greater and his inclination toward it stronger; and when inclination is always increasing while the attainment of the sought thing remains in one state, deprivation is inevitably necessary.

The third: He, exalted is He, said regarding the seeker of the tilth of the Hereafter, ﴿We shall increase for him in his tilth﴾, and did not mention whether He gives him this world or not, but the speech remained silent about it, affirmatively and negatively. As for the seeker of the tilth of this world, He explicitly stated that He does not give him any share of the Hereafter. This indicates a great disparity; as if He were saying: the Hereafter is the root and this world is the branch, so one who finds the root will find the branch to the extent of need. However, He did not mention that, as an alert that this world is too base to have its mention paired with the mention of the Hereafter.

The fourth: He, exalted is He, explained that the seeker of the Hereafter has his sought thing increased, and explained that the seeker of this world is given some of his sought thing from this world, but in the Hereafter he has absolutely no share. Thus by the first statement He showed that the state of the seeker of the Hereafter is always in ascent and increase, and by the second statement He showed that the state of the seeker of this world, in the first station, is in decline, and in the second station, in complete nullity.

The fifth: The Hereafter is credit (nasi'ah) and this world is cash (naqd), and credit is deemed inferior relative to cash, since people say: cash is better than credit. So He, exalted is He, showed that this judgment is reversed with respect to the states of the Hereafter and this world. The Hereafter, although it is credit, is oriented toward increase and permanence, so it is better and more perfect; and this world, although it is cash, is oriented toward decline and then toward nullity, so it is baser and more abject. This indicates that the state of the Hereafter does not at all resemble the state of this world, and that there is in this world of the states of the Hereafter nothing but the mere name, as is related from Ibn ʿAbbas.

The sixth: The verse indicates that the benefits of the Hereafter and this world are not immediately present; rather, in both realms tilth is necessary, and tilth cannot be accomplished except by bearing hardships in sowing, then watering, nurturing, harvesting, and then cleaning. So when God named both kinds "tilth," we knew that each of them is attained only by bearing toils and hardships. Then He explained that the outcome of the Hereafter is toward increase and perfection, and that the outcome of this world is toward decline and then annihilation. So it is as if it were said: if both kinds necessarily require bearing the toils of tilling, watering, nurturing, harvesting and cleaning, then it is more fitting that these toils be directed toward what is in increase and permanence than toward what is in decline, cessation and annihilation.

The second issue: Regarding His saying, ﴿We shall increase for him in his tilth﴾, there are two opinions:

The first: The meaning is that We increase in his success, his aid, and the facilitation of the paths of good deeds and acts of obedience for him. Muqatil said: ﴿We shall increase for him in his tilth﴾ by multiplying the reward. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿That He may pay them their rewards and increase them from His bounty﴾ [Fatir 35:30]. And it is related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Whoever rises in the morning with the concern of this world, Allah scatters his concern and places his poverty before his eyes, and what has not been written for him of this world does not come to him; and whoever rises in the morning with the concern of the Hereafter, Allah gathers his concern and places his richness in his heart, and this world comes to him while it is humbled." Or a wording close to this meaning.

The third issue: The apparent wording indicates that whoever prays for the sake of seeking reward or for the sake of averting punishment, his prayer is valid; but they have agreed that it is not valid. The answer: God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter﴾, and tilth cannot be achieved except by casting the correct seed into the earth, and the correct seed for all good things and felicities is nothing but the worship of Allah, exalted is He.

The fourth issue: Our companions said: if one performs ablution without intention, it is not valid. They said: because this person did not desire the tilth of the Hereafter, since the discussion concerns one who is heedless of the remembrance of Allah and of the Hereafter; therefore he must not obtain a share in what relates to the Hereafter, and discharging the obligation of prayer belongs to the category of the benefits of the Hereafter, so it must not be attained in ablution devoid of intention.

Know that when God, exalted is He, explained the greatest law and the most upright balance in the works of the Hereafter and this world, He followed it with an alert to what is fundamental in the domain of error and misery, so He said: ﴿Or do they have partners who have instituted for them in religion what Allah has not permitted?﴾ The meaning of the interrogative hamza in "am" is affirmation and rebuke. "Their partners" (shuraka'uhum) are their devils who adorned polytheism, the denial of resurrection, and working for this world, since they know nothing other than it. It was said: "their partners" are their idols; and they were attributed to them because they are the ones who took them as partners to Allah. And since they were the cause of their misguidance, they were made to legislate the religion of error, as Abraham ﷺ said: ﴿My Lord, they have led astray many of the people﴾ [Ibrahim 14:36]. And His saying, ﴿They have instituted for them in religion what Allah has not permitted﴾ means that all those laws are in opposition to Allah. Then He said: ﴿And were it not for the decisive word﴾, i.e., the prior decree to delay the recompense, or it is said: were it not for the promise that the decisive judgment would be on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿they would have been judged between them﴾, i.e., between the disbelievers and the believers, or between the polytheists and their partners. ﴿And indeed, the wrongdoers will have a painful punishment.﴾ Some read "wa-anna" with the hamza of "inna" opened, as a conjunction to "the decisive word," meaning: ﴿were it not for the decisive word﴾ and that their being punished in the Hereafter ﴿they would have been judged between them﴾ in this world. Then He, exalted is He, mentioned the states of the people of punishment and the states of the people of reward.

As for the first: it is His saying, ﴿You will see the wrongdoers fearful﴾, fearing intensely, ﴿of what they have earned﴾ of misdeeds, ﴿while it is going to befall them﴾; He means that its consequence is going to befall them, whether they feared or did not fear.

As for the second: it is the states of the people of reward, and it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in the gardens of Paradise﴾, because the garden of Paradise is the most pleasant spot in it. In the verse there is an alert that all the sinful people of the prayer are in Paradise, except that He specified those who believed and did righteous deeds for the gardens of Paradise, which are the noble spots of Paradise; so the spots below those gardens must necessarily be specified for those who were below those who believed and did righteous deeds. Then He said: ﴿They will have whatever they wish with their Lord﴾

This indicates that all things are present with Him, prepared. Then God, exalted is He, said in magnifying this rank: ﴿That is the great bounty.﴾ Our companions have used this verse to argue that reward is not obligatory upon Allah, but occurs by way of bounty from Allah, exalted is He. He said: ﴿Those who believed and did righteous deeds in the gardens of Paradise will have whatever they wish with their Lord﴾; this indicates that the gardens of Paradise and finding everything they desire is a recompense for faith and righteous deeds.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿That is the great bounty.﴾ This is an explicit statement that the recompense attached to deeds occurred by way of bounty, not by way of entitlement.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿That is what Allah gives good tidings of to His servants who believe and do righteous deeds.﴾ The author of al-Kashshaf said: it is read "yubashshiru" from "bashsharahu," "yubshiru" from "absharahu," and "yabshuru" from "bashara."

Know that these verses indicate the magnification of the state of reward in several respects:

The first: that Allah, glorified is He, attached to faith and righteous deeds the gardens of Paradise. A sovereign who is the greatest of beings and the most generous, when he attaches a recompense to arduous deeds, that indicates that this recompense has reached a point whose true nature none knows but Allah, exalted is He.

The second: He, exalted is He, said: ﴿They will have whatever they wish with their Lord﴾, and His saying ﴿They will have whatever they wish﴾ falls within the category of the infinite, because there is no rank except that a person desires what is higher than it.

The third: He, exalted is He, said: ﴿That is the great bounty﴾, and the one whose greatness is judged by He who has absolute majesty and grandeur is in utmost greatness.

The fourth: He, exalted is He, repeated the good tidings as a form of magnification, saying: ﴿That which Allah gives good tidings of to His servants﴾, and that also indicates the utmost grandeur. We ask Allah for success in them and for arrival at them.

Know that when He, exalted is He, revealed to Muhammad ﷺ this noble and exalted Book, and deposited in it the three categories: proofs, kinds of obligations, and attached reward to obedience and punishment to disobedience, He explained: I do not ask you, by means of this conveyance, for any immediate benefit or present gain, lest an ignorant person imagine that Muhammad's ﷺ purpose from this conveyance is wealth or status. So He said: ﴿Say, "I do not ask you for it any reward except affection for relatives."﴾ And in this there are issues:

The first issue: People have mentioned three opinions regarding this verse:

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 42, verses 20–26 (part 2 of 3):

First: al-Sha'bi said: "People argued with us about this verse, so we wrote to Ibn 'Abbas asking him about it. Ibn 'Abbas wrote that the Messenger of God ﷺ was the central point of lineage among the Quraysh, there being no clan (batn) of theirs to which he was not related by birth. So God said: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward﴾ for what I call you to, ﴿except﴾ that you show love to me because of my kinship with you. The meaning is: 'You are my people, and you are the most deserving of those who should respond to me and obey me. Since you have refused this, then at least preserve the right of kinship, do not harm me, and do not stir up opposition against me.'"

The second view: al-Kalbi narrated, "from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina, he was afflicted with calamities and obligations, and he had no means at his disposal. The Ansar said: 'This man has been guided by God through his hand, he is the son of your sister, and your neighbour in your city. So gather for him a portion of your wealth.' They did so, then brought it to him, but he returned it to them. Then the words of God, exalted is He, were revealed: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any reward for it﴾, that is, for faith, ﴿except that you love my relatives﴾. So He urged them to love his relatives."

[p. 142]

The third view: what al-Hasan mentioned, he said: "except that you show love (tawaddud) to God, through what brings you closer to Him, namely drawing near to Him through righteous deeds." So the word "al-qurba" (kinship) in the first view means blood-relationship (rahim), in the second it means the relatives themselves, and in the third it is a form (fu'la) from nearness (qurb) and bringing near (taqrib).

If it is said: the verse is problematic, because seeking a reward for conveying revelation is not permissible, and this is shown by several considerations:

First: God related of most of the prophets, peace be upon them, that they explicitly denied seeking any wage. He mentioned in the story of Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿And I ask you no reward for it; my reward is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 109]. Likewise in the stories of Hud and Salih, and in the stories of Lut and Shu'ayb, peace be upon them all. Our Prophet is more excellent than all the other prophets, peace be upon them, so it is more fitting that he should not seek a reward for prophethood and messengership.

Second: He ﷺ explicitly denied seeking a reward in other verses. He said: ﴿Say: whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours﴾ [Saba: 47], and he said: ﴿Say: I ask you no reward for it, and I am not one of the pretenders﴾ [Sad: 86].

Third: reason also indicates this, because that conveying was obligatory upon him. God said: ﴿Convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord, and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67]. And seeking a reward for performing an obligation is not fitting even for the least of people, let alone the most learned of scholars.

Fourth: prophethood is more excellent than wisdom (hikmah). God said of wisdom: ﴿And whoever is given wisdom has indeed been given much good﴾ [al-Baqarah: 269], and said of the worldly life: ﴿Say: the enjoyment of this world is little﴾ [al-Nisa: 77]. So how can it be reasonable to set the most noble of things against the basest of things?

Fifth: seeking a reward would give rise to suspicion, and that contradicts certainty in the soundness of prophethood.

By these considerations it is established that it is not permissible for the Prophet ﷺ to seek any reward at all for conveying and messengership. The apparent meaning of this verse, however, requires that he sought a reward for conveying and messengership, namely love in kinship. This is the statement of the objection. As for the answer: there is no dispute that it is not permissible to seek a reward for conveying and messengership. What remains is His words ﴿except love in kinship﴾. We say that the answer to it is in two ways:

The first: this is of the type of the poet's saying:

"There is no fault in them, except that their swords bear the notches of the armoured men's blows."

The meaning: "I ask nothing from you except this." But in reality this is not a reward, because the existence of love among Muslims is an obligation. God said: ﴿And the believing men and believing women are allies of one another﴾ [al-Tawbah: 71]. And he ﷺ said: "The believers are like a building, each part strengthening the others." The verses and reports on this theme are numerous. If the existence of love among the majority of Muslims is obligatory, then its existence toward the most noble and eminent of Muslims is more fitting. His words: ﴿Say: I ask you no reward for it, except love in kinship﴾, mean: "Love in kinship is not a reward," so the result returns to the conclusion that there is no reward at all.

The second answer: this is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati'), and the speech is complete at His words ﴿Say: I ask you no reward for it﴾. Then He said: ﴿except love in kinship﴾, meaning: "But I remind you of my kinship with you," and it appears in wording as a reward, but it is not a reward.

Third issue: the author of al-Kashshaf transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad dies as a martyr. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad dies forgiven. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad dies repentant. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad dies a believer whose faith is complete. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad, the Angel of Death gives him the good news of Paradise, then Munkar and Nakir. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad is escorted to Paradise as a bride is escorted to her husband's house. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad, two doors to Paradise are opened for him in his grave. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad,"

[p. 143]

"God makes his grave a place of visitation for the angels of mercy. Oh, and whoever dies upon love of the family of Muhammad dies upon the Sunnah and the Community. Oh, and whoever dies upon hatred of the family of Muhammad comes on the Day of Resurrection with 'despairing of God's mercy' written between his eyes. Oh, and whoever dies upon hatred of the family of Muhammad dies a disbeliever. Oh, and whoever dies upon hatred of the family of Muhammad will not smell the fragrance of Paradise." This is what the author of al-Kashshaf transmitted. As for me, I say: the family of Muhammad ﷺ are those whose affairs return to him. Whoever's affairs were most strongly and perfectly connected to him, those are the family (al-al). There is no doubt that Fatimah, 'Ali, al-Hasan and al-Husayn had the strongest connection with the Messenger of God ﷺ, and this is known by mass-transmitted (mutawatir) report. Therefore they must be the family. Also, people differed about the meaning of "al" (family). It was said: they are the kinsmen. It was said: they are his community. If we take it to mean kinsmen, then they are the family. If we take it to mean the community who accepted his call, then they too are family. So it is established that under all interpretations they are the family. As for others, whether they enter under the term "al", this is disputed.

The author of al-Kashshaf also transmitted that when this verse was revealed, "it was said: O Messenger of God, who are these relatives of yours whose love has become obligatory upon us? He said: 'Ali, Fatimah, and their two sons.'" Thus it is established that these four are relatives of the Prophet ﷺ, and when this is established, they must be singled out for greater honour. This is shown by several considerations:

First: His words ﴿except love in kinship﴾, and the way of deducing from it is what has preceded.

Second: There is no doubt that the Prophet ﷺ loved Fatimah, upon her be peace. He ﷺ said: "Fatimah is a part of me; whatever hurts her hurts me." And it is established by mass-transmitted report from the Messenger of God ﷺ that he loved 'Ali, al-Hasan and al-Husayn. If this is established, then it is obligatory upon the whole community to do likewise, by His words: ﴿Follow him, that you may be guided﴾ [al-A'raf: 158], and by His words: ﴿Let those who oppose his command beware﴾, and by His words: ﴿Say: if you love God, then follow me, and God will love you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 31], and by His words, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed there is for you in the Messenger of God an excellent example﴾ [al-Ahzab: 21].

Third: invoking blessings upon the family is a great station, and for this reason this supplication was made the closing part of the tashahhud in prayer, namely: "O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, and have mercy upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad." This honour has not been found for anyone other than the family. All of this shows that love for the family of Muhammad is obligatory. Al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him, said:

"O rider, halt at al-Muhassab in Mina, and call out to the one who dwells in its valley and the one who rises up,
at dawn when the pilgrims pour out toward Mina, in a flow like the overflowing of the Euphrates,
If loving the family of Muhammad is rafd (rejection), then let both jinn and men bear witness that I am a rafidi."

The fourth issue: His words ﴿except love in kinship﴾ contain a great station for the Companions, because He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the foremost, the foremost, those are the ones brought near﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 10–11]. So everyone who obeyed God was brought near to God, exalted is He, and therefore enters under His words ﴿except love in kinship﴾. The conclusion: this verse indicates the obligation of loving the family of the Messenger of God ﷺ and loving his Companions. This station is not secure except according to our companions, the people of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah), who combined love for the progeny (al-'itrah) and love for the Companions. I heard some of those mentioned say that he ﷺ said: "The likeness of my family is like the ark of Noah: whoever boarded it was saved." He ﷺ also said: "My Companions are like the stars; whichever of them you follow, you will be guided." We are now in the sea of obligation, and the waves of doubts and desires strike us, and the one who rides the sea needs two things:

One of them: a ship free of defects and holes.
